title: Early Changes in Peripancreatic Mesenteric Fat Beyond Weight Loss Predict Durability of Hepatic Improvements in MASLD.
abstract: Aims Various visceral adipose tissue depots exhibit heterogeneous metabolic properties. This study aims to explore whether specific abdominal fat compartments differentially predict loss of sustained treatment response to lifestyle interventions in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Materials and methods Consecutive treatment-naïve MASLD patients were prospectively enrolled from January 2015 to March 2024, with a 96-week follow-up period. Liver fat content, preperitoneal fat thickness (PFT), peripancreatic mesenteric fat thickness (MFT1), periumbilical mesenteric fat thickness (MFT2) and perirenal fat thickness (PrFT) were quantified using magnetic resonance imaging. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) was assessed by 2D-SWE. Treatment responses were evaluated at 48 and 96 weeks, and the primary outcome was loss of response at 96 weeks. Results A total of 631 MASLD patients (mean age: 41.5 ± 13.8 years; 72.0% male) were included. Logistic regression analyses revealed that a greater 48-week relative decrease in MFT1 (per 10% relative reduction), rather than in MFT2, PFT or PrFT, was independently associated with lower odds of losing MRI-PDFF response (OR: 0.48, 95% CI: 0.34-0.69, p < 0.001) and LSM response (OR: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.28-0.99, p = 0.046) at 96 weeks. Receiver operating characteristic curve analyses indicated that relative changes in MFT1 showed discriminatory ability for the loss of MRI-PDFF and LSM responses, with areas under the curves of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.64-0.76) and 0.77 (95% CI: 0.67-0.88), respectively. Conclusions Early changes in MFT1 were associated with subsequent loss of response in hepatic steatosis and fibrosis, suggesting potential prognostic value for hepatic response durability in MASLD.

title: Multimodal Echocardiography for Assessing Left Ventricular Function: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Background Left ventricular (LV) function occupies a central position in cardiovascular health and disease, and its accurate noninvasive evaluation has accordingly attracted sustained investigative interest. In recent years, a succession of emerging echocardiographic techniques has expanded the scope of LV function evaluation beyond conventional volumetric parameters. These advances collectively enable a multidimensional characterization of cardiac anatomy, mechanics, perfusion, and microcirculation. Within this evolving paradigm, multimodal echocardiography represents a promising framework for comprehensive evaluation of LV function and forms the subject of the present review. Scope and approach This review summarizes the principles and recent advances of three-dimensional echocardiography (3DE), speckle tracking echocardiography (STE), contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), and super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) in LV function assessment, together with their representative clinical applications, the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) in multimodal fusion, and the translational challenges toward clinical practice. Key findings and conclusions Current evidence indicates that these techniques extend LV function assessment beyond conventional parameters, affording geometry-independent volumetric quantification, sensitive detection of subclinical myocardial dysfunction, quantitative evaluation of microcirculatory perfusion, and direct visualization of myocardial microvessels. These technologies span a spectrum of validation and clinical adoption, ranging from established applications recommended for routine use in guidelines, through selected specialist applications, to experimental approaches that remain at the stage of feasibility validation or conceptual design. Although operator dependence, cross-platform variability, and the absence of standardized protocols remain major barriers to the routine application of the latter two categories of technologies, the complementarity of these modalities yields mechanistic and prognostic insights that no single technique can provide in isolation. Continued advances must be matched by validation in large-scale, multicenter, prospective studies. Only then can multimodal echocardiography deliver the noninvasive, multiscale, and integrated assessment of LV function.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Echocardiographic Platform for Automated Measurements in Children.
abstract: Purpose This study assessed the accuracy of a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted echocardiographic platform for automated measurements in children. Methods In this prospective, blinded, comparative, single-center pilot study, transthoracic echocardiography was performed in pediatric subjects aged 5 to 18 years using the Siemens Acuson Origin cardiovascular ultrasound system. For spectral Doppler assessments, two echocardiographic acquisitions were required: one using the AI-assisted protocol with automatic spectral Doppler marker placement, and one with manual marker placement. For all other analyses, a single manual acquisition was required for subsequent AI and manual assessments. Images were initially analyzed with the AI-assisted protocol, followed immediately by manual evaluation by a pediatric cardiologist blinded to the AI-derived results. Indices included B-mode, M-mode, Doppler, speckle tracking, and four-dimensional (4D) parameters. Agreement between AI-assisted and manual measurements was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis. Results Thirty subjects (23 males; age 12.2±3.8 years) were studied, including 23 with structurally normal heart, six with congenital heart diseases, and one with dilated cardiomyopathy. Feasibility exceeded 90% for 2D AI-assisted assessment and 80% for 4D ventricular volumetry, but was below 35% for 4D atrial volumetry. Agreement between AI-assisted and manual measurements was strong for all parameters except septal (ICC 0.2) and left ventricular posterior wall thickness (ICC 0.5). Bland-Altman analysis showed no significant systematic differences. Conclusion Our pilot findings suggest that a commercially available AI-assisted echocardiographic system may be feasible and reasonably accurate for conventional and advanced quantitative echocardiographic assessment for children in a real-world setting.

title: Multistructural Cardiac Damage Staging in Chronic Aortic Regurgitation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Purpose To assess whether independently developed cardiac-damage staging systems identify concordant mortality associations in chronic aortic regurgitation (AR), without assuming equivalence of stage definitions. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and Web of Science were searched through September 16, 2026 for longitudinal cohorts of adults with native moderate or greater AR. Adjusted all-cause mortality hazard ratios (HRs) were summarized using exploratory random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp inference. Results Five cohorts comprised 6043 patients; four used predominantly echocardiographic staging and one used a magnetic resonance-led multimodality framework. One cohort contributed 4026 patients, 78% of whom had moderate AR. The exploratory pooled HR per study-defined stage was 1.72 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09-2.71; three cohorts, n = 1446; I 2 = 62.7%). Restricting this analysis to two four-category frameworks yielded an HR of 1.90 (95% CI, 0.48-7.52; n = 827). For selected source-defined downstream categories versus no damage, the pooled HR was 2.89 (95% CI, 1.63-5.12; three cohorts, n = 4992; I 2 = 0%). Three studies reported incremental prognostic performance. Staging definitions and valve-intervention handling differed across studies. Conclusion Independently developed frameworks identified adverse mortality associations in mixed moderate-to-severe AR populations. Pooled HRs are exploratory summaries of nonequivalent exposures and follow-up strategies; they do not validate a universal staging scale, severe AR-specific risk stratification, or an intervention threshold.

Five cohorts comprised 6043 patients; four used predominantly echocardiographic staging and one used a magnetic resonance-led multimodality framework. One cohort contributed 4026 patients, 78% of whom had moderate AR. The exploratory pooled HR per study-defined stage was 1.72 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09-2.71; three cohorts, n = 1446; I2 = 62.7%). Restricting this analysis to two four-category frameworks yielded an HR of 1.90 (95% CI, 0.48-7.52; n = 827). For selected source-defined downstream categories versus no damage, the pooled HR was 2.89 (95% CI, 1.63-5.12; three cohorts, n = 4992; I2 = 0%). Three studies reported incremental prognostic performance. Staging definitions and valve-intervention handling differed across studies.

Conclusion

Independently developed frameworks identified adverse mortality associations in mixed moderate-to-severe AR populations. Pooled HRs are exploratory summaries of nonequivalent exposures and follow-up strategies; they do not validate a universal staging scale, severe AR-specific risk stratification, or an intervention threshold.

title: Diagnostic Performance of Photon-Counting Coronary CT Angiography in Patients Undergoing TAVI: A Comparison With Invasive Angiography.
abstract: Background Since coronary artery disease (CAD) is common in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), invasive coronary angiography (ICA) is performed in preparation for the procedure, although many patients do not require coronary intervention. Photon-counting Computed Tomography (PCCT) offers improved spatial resolution compared with conventional energy-integrating detector CT. The aim of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic performance of PCCT for the detection of significant CAD in patients undergoing TAVI evaluation using ICA as the reference standard. Methods In this single-center study, 201 consecutive patients undergoing preprocedural TAVI work-up with both PCCT and ICA were included. Sensitivity, specificity, and positive and negative predictive values (PPV and NPV) were calculated at ≥ 50% and ≥ 70% stenosis thresholds using recorded binary classifications. Non-evaluable coronary territories were considered CT-positive. Patient-level 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were exact binomial; vessel-level CIs used patient-cluster bootstrap resampling. Results Of 201 patients were included (mean age 79.6 ± 7.2 years; 118 [58.7%] male). Image quality was excellent or good in 167 patients (83.1%). On ICA, ≥ 50% stenoses were present in 126 patients (62.7%) and ≥ 70% stenoses in 114 (56.7%). For ≥ 50% stenosis, per-patient sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV were 98.4% (95% CI, 94.4%-99.8%), 93.3% (85.1%-97.8%), 96.1% (91.2%-98.7%), and 97.2% (90.3%-99.7%), respectively. Corresponding values for ≥ 70% stenosis were 99.1% (95.2%-100.0%), 89.7% (81.3%-95.2%), 92.6% (86.5%-96.6%), and 98.7% (93.1%-100.0%). At the ≥ 50% threshold, 72 patients (35.8%) were CT-negative; 70 were true negatives and two were false negatives. Conclusions PCCT demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy for the detection and exclusion of significant CAD in patients undergoing TAVI evaluation. PCCT coronary angiography may serve as a non-invasive gatekeeper to invasive coronary angiography and support a more efficient pre-procedural workflow.

title: Regenerative Endodontic Treatment in Traumatized Immature Permanent Teeth: How Predictable Is the Outcome?
abstract: Pulp necrosis following traumatic dental injury in an immature permanent tooth interrupts root development, leaving thin dentinal walls and an open apex that compromise long-term tooth survival. Conventional apexification can predictably achieve apical barrier formation and periapical healing but does not promote continued root maturation. Regenerative endodontic treatment (RET) was developed to address this biological limitation. Two decades of experimental and clinical research have established the biological rationale and clinical potential of RET. Current evidence indicates that RET generally achieves its primary goal of periapical healing. However, its secondary goal-continued root development, including increased root length and dentinal wall thickness-is considerably less predictable. Radiographic root maturation varies substantially and does not necessarily translate into improved long-term tooth survival. The tertiary goal, recovery of pulp sensibility, is also inconsistently achieved, and predictable regeneration of a functional pulp-dentin complex has yet to be demonstrated. The aim of this mini-review was to synthesize the current evidence on the biological basis, clinical protocols, outcomes, adverse events, and long-term prognosis of RET in traumatized immature permanent teeth, with particular emphasis on treatment predictability. Three clinically and biologically distinct outcomes are distinguished: resolution of apical disease, continued root development, and true tissue regeneration. By integrating clinical and translational evidence, we identify what can reasonably be expected from RET, where uncertainty remains, and which factors may influence long-term outcomes. RET outcomes appear to be influenced by trauma severity, pre-operative apical periodontitis, and antimicrobial effectiveness. Periapical healing is the most consistently achieved outcome, whereas continued root maturation is less predictable, and regeneration of a functional pulp-dentin complex has not been demonstrated clinically. Whether RET provides a long-term survival advantage over apexification remains uncertain. Much of the available evidence derives from mixed populations of traumatic and developmental etiologies, and trauma-related pulp necrosis is associated with poorer continued root maturation.

title: Cognitive Cerebellum Structure and Functional Connectivity in Relation to Executive Functions in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) has been primarily linked to abnormalities within the cortico-striato-thalamo-cortical circuit; however, recent evidence suggests that the posterior cerebellum may contribute to the executive dysfunction observed in the disorder. In 56 adults (28 OCD, 28 controls), we assessed executive functions using the BANFE-2 battery and integrated structural MRI (T1) and resting-state fMRI. Although the Global Executive Index did not differ significantly between groups, patients with OCD showed significantly lower scores in the inhibitory control/decision-making domain relative to controls. We quantified cortical thickness and volume (% intracranial volume) in Crus I/II and lobule VI using CERES and examined resting-state functional connectivity (seed-to-voxel) in CONN, adjusting for age, sex, medication, and depression. Compared with controls, patients with OCD showed reduced bilateral cortical thickness in Crus I/II and lobule VI (false discovery rate-corrected q < 0.05; β_OCD - Control = -0.27 to -0.59; ηp 2 = 0.34-0.55), with no significant volumetric differences after correction for multiple comparisons. Functional connectivity results revealed a mixed pattern, including focal hyperconnectivity (e.g., left Crus I with primary auditory cortex; left Crus II with occipital cortex) and widespread intracerebellar hypoconnectivity. In addition, significant Group × executive-function interactions (p-family-wise error < 0.05) emerged mainly for bilateral Crus I (Global Executive Index and working memory/flexibility) and left lobule VI (inhibition/decision-making), indicating that the relationship between cerebellar connectivity and executive performance differs in OCD relative to controls. These findings support an expanded model of executive circuits in OCD that incorporates the posterior cerebellum as a relevant node.

title: Nonlinear Dopaminergic Vulnerability and Incident Freezing of Gait in Parkinson Disease: Limited Incremental Value of Global Volumetric MRI.
abstract: Freezing of gait is a disabling manifestation of Parkinson disease, but it remains uncertain how risk varies across the spectrum of nigrostriatal dopaminergic loss and whether global volumetric magnetic resonance imaging adds prognostic information. We analyzed longitudinal Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative data from participants who remained free of recorded freezing through completion of a temporally aligned multimodal imaging index. The cohort comprised 521 participants with 251 incident recorded events; 520 participants and 250 events contributed to adjusted models. Lower mean striatal specific binding ratio was associated with subsequent recorded freezing after adjustment for age, sex, and motor severity (hazard ratio per one-standard-deviation increase, 0.740; 95% confidence interval, 0.613-0.894; p = 0.002). Restricted cubic splines showed evidence of a nonlinear association (p < 0.001), with risk rising disproportionately at lower binding; relative to the median, the adjusted hazard was 2.52 (95% confidence interval, 1.72-3.69) at the 5th percentile. Regional analyses localized this pattern predominantly to the putamen. Nonlinear representation improved model fit compared with linear dopaminergic modelling (likelihood-ratio χ 2 = 13.78; 2 degrees of freedom; p = 0.001) and increased Harrell concordance from 0.627 to 0.649, although the bootstrap confidence interval for this increment included zero. Three-year discrimination improved from 0.643 to 0.682. Adding ventricular ratio did not improve fit or discrimination, and the optimism-corrected concordance statistic was 0.633. These findings support a cohort-specific threshold-like dopaminergic vulnerability pattern, predominantly putaminal, whereas global volumetric MRI added negligible incremental prognostic information, and model performance remained insufficient for individual clinical prediction. The nonlinear functional form requires external replication.

title: Convergence of Cerebrospinal Fluid Neuronal Biomarker Burden and MRI Lesion Pattern and Its Association With Short-Term Outcome in Neuroinfectious Diseases.
abstract: Background Neuroinfectious diseases (NDs) are potentially treatable conditions associated with substantial morbidity, but their clinical course remains difficult to predict. While specific MRI patterns are characteristic of distinct aetiologies, their prognostic value remains poorly investigated. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers of neuroaxonal and synaptic damage have been linked to clinical outcome. We investigated the association of CSF biomarkers and MRI findings with short-term outcome in NDs. Methods In this multicentre cohort study, CSF was analysed in 123 patients with NDs and in 95 non-neuroinflammatory controls. Concentrations of beta-synuclein, SNAP-25, neurogranin and neurofilament light chain protein (NfL) were measured. MRI findings were classified by topography and lesion pattern. Clinical outcome at discharge was assessed using the modified Rankin Scale and degree of recovery. Results All CSF biomarkers were higher in ND patients with MRI abnormalities than in those without MRI abnormalities and/or controls, also within the (meningo-)encephalitis group. Temporal lobe involvement was the MRI pattern most consistently associated with elevated CSF biomarkers, even after multivariable adjustment including aetiology, and was independently associated with poor functional outcome and incomplete recovery. A global neuronal biomarker burden derived by principal component analysis (PC1) improved the fit of outcome models including MRI lesion pattern, with both temporal lobe involvement and PC1 remaining independently associated with outcome at discharge. Conclusions MRI lesion pattern and CSF biomarkers of synaptic and neuroaxonal damage were independently associated with short-term outcome in NDs, suggesting that they capture complementary aspects of disease severity. Prospective studies are needed to establish their prognostic value.

title: The CoMPaSS-NMD Atlas Platform: A Secure Multimodal Infrastructure for Harmonized Data Collection, Exploration, and Future Artificial Intelligence-Driven Stratification in Hereditary Neuromuscular Disorders.
abstract: Background Hereditary neuromuscular disorders exhibit marked phenotypic and molecular heterogeneity, which weakens genotype-phenotype correlation and complicates timely diagnosis, prognosis, and patient stratification for clinical trials. The Horizon Europe project CoMPaSS-NMD aims to develop artificial-intelligence-based stratification tools by integrating clinical, genetic, histopathological, and imaging data from clinical reference centers across Europe and the United Kingdom. Methods We developed CoMPaSS-NMD Atlas, a secure, modular web platform for pseudonymized data collection, multimodal data management, and controlled exploration. Clinical, technical, and data-management experts defined requirements; contributing centers co-designed electronic clinical and histopathology forms. Clinical phenotypes used the Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO), while imaging, histopathology, and sequencing data followed international standards. Results The platform supports role- and attribute-based access, pseudonymized patient registration, metadata management, structured clinical data entry, MRI and histopathological uploads, and a dedicated genetic-sequencing workflow. Cohort-level exploration is driven by structured metadata and HPO terms, enabling hierarchical phenotype navigation, ontology-aware data navigation, and cross-domain queries spanning clinical, genetic, imaging, and histopathological features. Users can download raw files in their original formats, along with structured metadata reports in CSV or PDF, according to the permissions defined for data protection. Conclusions The Atlas provides a foundation for harmonized, standardized prospective data collection and for building large datasets for artificial intelligence- and machine learning-based patient stratification. With secure governance, traceability, and multimodal integration, it is designed to support diagnostic and stratification research in hereditary neuromuscular disorders; clinical validation is ongoing.

title: Evaluating Predictors of Tumor in Patients With Anti-GABA-B Receptor Encephalitis.
abstract: Objective Anti-GABA-B receptor encephalitis is a rare but severe autoimmune encephalitis subtype with a close association with malignancy, particularly small-cell lung cancer. This study aimed to characterize tumor-associated clinical features and identify practical warning signs for tumor occurrence in patients with anti-GABA-B receptor encephalitis. Methods We retrospectively enrolled 66 consecutive patients diagnosed with anti-GABA-B receptor encephalitis between July 2013 and July 2025. Demographic characteristics, clinical manifestations, cerebrospinal fluid and serum findings, neuroimaging and electroencephalographic features, tumor-screening results, treatment, and outcomes were compared between patients with and without tumors. Results Among 66 patients, 38 (57.6%) were diagnosed with tumors, including 36 with small-cell lung cancer. The tumor group was older (p = 0.021) and more frequently presented with sleep disorders (33/38, 86.8% vs. 18/28, 64.3%, p = 0.031), decreased consciousness (27/38, 71.1% vs. 13/28, 46.4%, p = 0.043), and hyponatremia (22/38, 57.9% vs. 9/28, 32.1%, p = 0.038). Serum paraneoplastic antibodies were more common in patients with tumors, and tumor markers including NSE (16/34, 47.1% vs 0/24, 0%, p < 0.001) and ProGRP (23/34, 67.6% vs 3/24, 12.5%, p < 0.001) were more frequently elevated. AI-assisted CT analysis provided additional support for lung cancer screening. During follow-up, patients with tumors had poorer outcomes (p < 0.001) and higher mortality (p < 0.001). Conclusion Advanced age, severe clinical presentation, elevated tumor markers, and coexisting serum paraneoplastic antibodies may help identify patients who require intensive and repeated tumor screening. AI-assisted CT diagnostic techniques may further improve early lung cancer detection, but prospective validation is required.

title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

title: Cone-beam computed tomography voxel size and diagnostic accuracy across endodontic tasks: A systematic review.
abstract: Selecting an appropriate cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) voxel protocol is clinically relevant for detecting subtle endodontic abnormalities, yet diagnostic performance depends on more than nominal voxel dimensions. This systematic review synthesized evidence on vertical root fractures, second mesiobuccal canals, external root resorption, and root perforations. Six information sources yielded 683 records; 16 ex vivo studies met the eligibility criteria. Published sensitivity, specificity, and area-under-the-curve findings were verified and synthesized by task, scanner, material condition, and voxel protocol; no meta-analysis was retained because reliable independent comparisons were insufficient. Seven studies addressed root fractures, three additional canals, four external resorption, and two perforations. In individual experiments, finer protocols improved sensitivity for certain fractures and perforations, whereas filling materials, artifacts, treatment stage, lesion location, and scanner settings modified performance. Certainty for laboratory diagnostic accuracy was low for fractures and resorption and very low for canal detection and perforations; clinical extrapolation was very low across tasks. The findings support clinically useful, indication-led selection of CBCT protocols, emphasizing diagnostically adequate image detail, restricted field of view, and exposure optimization rather than a universally preferred voxel size.

title: CDKN1A Mediates Regulated Cell Death in Osteoblasts and Exacerbates Periapical Bone Destruction in Apical Periodontitis.
abstract: Background Apical periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory bone-destructive disease driven by intracanal microbial infection and host immune-inflammatory responses. Periapical bone destruction arises not only from excessive osteoclastic resorption but also from osteoblast dysfunction and dysregulated regulated cell death (RCD). CDKN1A (p21) is a canonical cell-cycle regulator implicated in multiple RCD programs, yet its role in osteoblast injury and apical periodontitis pathogenesis remains undefined. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing (ScRNA) was used to profile osteoblast subpopulations and RCD-related gene expression in human periapical lesions. Porphyromonas gingivalis infection models were established in MG63 and MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts, and DIA proteomics and western blot were used to evaluate RCD-related proteins. The effects of CDKN1A, a disease-associated hub gene screened out in DIA proteomics, on RCD-related proteins were further examined by western blot. Lentiviral silencing and AAV-mediated overexpression were performed in vitro and in rat apical periodontitis models. Bone destruction, RCD activation and osteogenic capacity were assessed by micro-CT, histomorphology and multiplex immunofluorescence. Results ScRNA data of apical periodontitis showed that osteoblasts in apical lesions exhibited enhanced apoptosis and pyroptosis and reduced ferroptosis. Single-bacteria P. gingivalis infection markedly upregulated CDKN1A, which promoted osteoblast apoptosis and pyroptosis while suppressing necroptosis and ferroptosis. In vivo, CDKN1A expression increased with disease progression and was negatively correlated with the osteogenic marker OPN. CDKN1A overexpression aggravated bone destruction, whereas its knockdown significantly attenuated bone loss and restored osteogenic activity. Conclusion CDKN1A acts as a critical regulator that mediates RCD of osteoblasts, impairs osteogenesis and exacerbates periapical bone destruction in apical periodontitis. Targeting CDKN1A-mediated RCD represents a promising therapeutic strategy to limit bone destruction and promote repair in apical periodontitis.

title: Clinical Diagnosis Versus Plain Radiography for Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis: A Prospective Study of Diagnostic Agreement in a Resource-Limited Settings.
abstract: Diabetic foot osteomyelitis (DFO) is a serious complication of diabetic foot ulcers, particularly in advanced infections. In low-resource settings, access to medical imaging may be limited. This study evaluated the diagnostic agreement between a composite clinical approach (clinical assessment plus probe-to-bone test) compared with plain radiography for diagnosing DFO, including performance across ulcer categories. A prospective cohort study was conducted from December 2021 to January 2025 among patients with suspected DFO. Participants underwent clinical evaluation, risk factor assessment, ulcer history, SINBAD classification, probe-to-bone testing and plain radiography. Diagnostic performance measures were calculated. Given the absence of a gold standard reference test (bone biopsy) in this low-resource setting, performance measures represent comparative diagnostic agreement with plain radiography rather than absolute diagnostic accuracy. A total of 166 patients with deep foot ulcers were enrolled. Composite clinical diagnosis identified osteomyelitis in 117 patients and excluded it in 49. Plain radiography was positive in 96 of 117 composite positive cases, while 21 were discordant; all 49 composite negative cases were radiographically negative. The composite approach showed 100% sensitivity, 70% specificity and 87.3% overall agreement. Sensitivity remained 100% across ulcer categories, while specificity increased significantly from 63.8% in SINBAD-4 ulcers to 77.8% in SINBAD-5 ulcers, improving agreement from 86.1% to 89.7%. In conclusion, composite clinical diagnosis demonstrates substantial agreement with plain radiography in this cohort of patients with suspected DFO. This can provide a practical adjunct for clinical assessment in resource-limited settings where imaging is unavailable or difficult to interpret but should not be considered a definitive diagnostic test in the absence of an independent reference standard.

title: Implantation Technique, Continuous Implant Geometry, and Longitudinal Low-Voltage Impedance After Subcutaneous Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Implantation.
abstract: Background Defibrillation efficacy of the subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (S-ICD) depends on shock vector geometry and tissue impedances influenced by implantation technique. Whether longitudinal low-voltage impedance (LVI) measurements differ across contemporary implantation strategies, and whether these differences are explained by quantitative radiographic geometry, remains incompletely characterized. Objective To determine whether S-ICD implantation technique is associated with longitudinal LVI trajectories and whether continuous radiographic implant geometry provides information beyond categorical PRAETORIAN risk classification. Methods We performed a single-center retrospective cohort study of 136 adults receiving an S-ICD between 2014 and 2024, classified by operative documentation as subcutaneous (SC; n = 27), fluoroscopy-marked intermuscular (FIM; n = 73), or fluoroscopy-marked ultrasound-guided intermuscular (FUSIM; n = 36) techniques. Per-device LVI was summarized overall and across prespecified windows (0-30 days, 6 months-1 year, 2-5 years). Technique differences were analyzed. We fit a prespecified mixed-effects interaction model that included coil-sternum distance, scaled in 5 mm increments, and assessed correlations between LVI and radiographic measures. Results In paired analyses, LVI increased by a mean of 13.3 Ω between the 0-30-day and 2-5-year windows. Overall LVI differed by implantation technique (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.019), driven by higher values in SC versus FIM (Holm-adjusted p = 0.041) and FUSIM (p = 0.022). Additional impedance differences across techniques were absent in the 0-30-day window but emerged during follow-up. In the prespecified interaction mixed-effects model, SC exhibited a significant additional rise relative to FUSIM during the 2-5-year window (interaction β = 7.82 Ω, 95% CI 0.98-14.67; p = 0.025). Greater coil-sternum distance was independently associated with higher LVI (13.6 Ω per cm, 95% CI 4.2-23.0; p = 0.005) and correlated with chronic LVI (n = 76; r = 0.441; Benjamini-Hochberg q < 0.001). The PRAETORIAN score was computable in 76 devices and classified 84% as low risk; within that low-risk stratum, coil-sternum distance remained associated with chronic LVI (ρ = 0.320, p = 0.010) whereas the score did not (ρ = 0.136, p = 0.282), and each 5 mm of coil-sternum distance corresponded to 10.7 Ω higher LVI after adjustment for BMI (95% CI 2.68-18.73, p = 0.010). High-voltage shock impedance at implant correlated strongly with chronic LVI (n = 99; r = 0.71, p < 0.001), and the association persisted over 2-5 years (n = 69; r = 0.61, p < 0.001). Conclusion Longitudinal LVI varies with S-ICD implantation strategy, with time-dependent divergence between SC and intermuscular implants. Within the low-risk PRAETORIAN category, where the categorical score has no dynamic range, continuously measured coil-sternum distance remains associated with chronic impedance. Continuous implant geometry and longitudinal impedance complement, rather than replace, radiographic scoring of implant position.

title: The Role of Extracardiac Uptake in [ 99 mTc]Tc-DPD Scintigraphy in Patients With ATTRwt.
abstract: Background and aims Quantification of the soft tissue uptake in 99m Tc-DPD has emerged as a promising imaging biomarker in ATTRwt. Recent findings suggest a potential role of [ 99m Tc]Tc-DPD soft tissue uptake in the diagnosis of polyneuropathy in these patients. Methods In this registry study, we analyzed all patients who presented at the Amyloidosis Centre Berlin and underwent a standardized diagnostic protocol comprising a multidisciplinary examination, neuroelectrophysiology, ECG, biomarkers, [ 99m Tc]Tc-DPD scintigraphy and echocardiography, without other causes of polyneuropathy. We analyzed the planar scans using soft-tissue-to-bone and heart-to-hemithorax ratios. We assessed the subcutaneous fat uptake using SUVmean derived from SPECT/CT. Results Of the 72 patients, 57 ATTRwt patients were included in the analysis. Among these, the prevalence of polyneuropathy and cardiomyopathy was 60% and 95%, respectively. The neurographic pattern was mainly axonal (53%) or mixed (32%). Patients with polyneuropathy showed significantly higher SUVmean in axillary subcutaneous tissue compared to those without (p-value = 0.002). There was no correlation between extracardiac tracer uptake and polyneuropathy severity by using the NIS. Interpretation Our results indicate that amyloid load in soft tissue may serve as a potential indicator of peripheral neurological involvement. Future studies are required to explore the utility of DPD scintigraphy for outcome assessment in treated patients.

title: Efficacy and Safety of High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound for Aesthetic Contouring and Skin Tightening: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Introduction High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) has emerged as a prominent non-invasive modality for aesthetic contouring and skin tightening, targeting localized adiposity and skin laxity through thermal coagulation, acoustic cavitation, and adipocyte disruption. This systematic review comprehensively evaluates the clinical efficacy and safety of HIFU for aesthetic body rejuvenation and cervicofacial skin tightening in adults. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of MEDLINE, Scopus, and the Cochrane CENTRAL database was conducted for English-language clinical studies published between 2010 and 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials and observational studies reporting quantitative outcomes for HIFU for fat reduction, circumferential reduction, skin tightening, cellulite improvement, or cervicofacial lifting outcomes. Results Sixty studies met the eligibility criteria. Fat-thickness reductions were approximately 2.2-9.0 mm and circumference reductions approximately 1-4 cm. Cellulite severity decreased by 1.61 points, with physician-rated aesthetic improvement of 81.5%-89.5% at 3-6 months. Laxity outcomes showed reductions of approximately 0.48-1.15 across facial, cervical, and abdominal regions, while cervicofacial studies reported brow elevation up to approximately 2 mm and a mean submental lift of 26.44 mm 2 at 3 months. Adverse events were predominantly mild and transient. Methodological heterogeneity and risk of bias limited certainty across outcomes. Conclusion HIFU may provide a noninvasive option for body contouring, skin tightening, and cervicofacial rejuvenation, with generally favorable changes across objective and patient-reported outcomes. More standardized comparative studies are needed to better define the magnitude and durability of treatment-related changes. Trial registration PROSPERO (CRD420251239376).

This systematic review comprehensively evaluates the clinical efficacy and safety of HIFU for aesthetic body rejuvenation and cervicofacial skin tightening in adults.

Methods

Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of MEDLINE, Scopus, and the Cochrane CENTRAL database was conducted for English-language clinical studies published between 2010 and 2025. Eligible studies included randomized controlled trials and observational studies reporting quantitative outcomes for HIFU for fat reduction, circumferential reduction, skin tightening, cellulite improvement, or cervicofacial lifting outcomes.

Sixty studies met the eligibility criteria. Fat-thickness reductions were approximately 2.2-9.0 mm and circumference reductions approximately 1-4 cm. title: Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Technical Advances, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Radiotherapy is an essential treatment modality for cervical cancer and has evolved substantially with advances in image guidance and treatment delivery. This review summarizes recent technological developments in external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy, their clinical applications, and future directions, with particular consideration of Japanese practice in an international context. In external beam radiotherapy, conventional techniques incorporating central shielding are increasingly being replaced by intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) and volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT). Daily three-dimensional image-guided radiotherapy (3D-IGRT) is essential for the safe implementation of these techniques because of substantial uterine motion and deformation. In brachytherapy, the transition from two-dimensional point-based prescription to three-dimensional image-guided treatment has enabled individualized assessment of target coverage and doses to organs at risk. Although magnetic resonance imaging-based brachytherapy is internationally recommended, computed tomography-based planning predominates in Japan and has achieved favorable outcomes, despite some studies reporting lower cumulative target doses than those recommended internationally. Intracavitary/interstitial brachytherapy (IC/IS BT) further improves dose distribution by combining intracavitary applicators with interstitial needles, particularly when adequate target coverage cannot be achieved with standard intracavitary brachytherapy alone. Future advances may include artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted treatment planning and adaptive workflows, tissue spacers to overcome anatomical constraints, and the incorporation of genomic, multi-omics, and radiomics information. Integrating these approaches may enable cervical cancer radiotherapy to progress beyond increasingly safe and precise treatment toward personalized care tailored to individual patient and tumor characteristics.

title: Hidden in Plain Sight: A Case Report of a Rare Subserous Uterine Adenomyoma Mimicking an Ovarian Cyst With Literature Review.
abstract: The uterine corpus adenomyoma is a benign mixed epithelial and mesenchymal tumor, classified by the World Health Organization, fifth edition (2020), as a distinct lesion composed of endometrioid-type glands, endometrioid-type stroma, and smooth muscle. Subserosal adenomyomas with a pedunculated polypoid configuration represent a rare morphological presentation. We describe the case of a 46-year-old woman who presented for surgical evaluation of a right ovarian mass. Preoperative investigations, including transvaginal pelvic ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), showed a right adnexal cystic lesion. The patient underwent robot-assisted laparoscopy that suggested a subserosal cystic adenomyoma of the posterior uterine wall, a diagnosis confirmed by histological examination. This case underscores the importance of detailed intraoperative and pathological assessment for diagnosing pedunculated subserosal adenomyoma, which may be misdiagnosed clinically or radiologically. In similar situations, it is essential to consider the possibility of a subserosal adenomyoma to ensure appropriate preoperative counseling for the patient.

title: Predictive Value of the Helsinki CT Score in Traumatic Brain Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background and purpose The Helsinki CT score integrates multiple radiographic features for prognostic assessment after traumatic brain injury (TBI), but its predictive performance varies across studies. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated its ability to predict mortality and unfavorable functional outcomes in patients with TBI. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched up to May 10, 2026. Cohort studies evaluating the Helsinki CT score for predicting outcomes in TBI were included. A random-effects model was used to pool the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and subgroup analyses were performed according to outcome assessment timing and CT score types. Results Fifteen studies (n = 10,569) were included. The pooled AUC of the Helsinki CT score was 0.80 (n = 10; 95% CI: 0.76-0.83) for mortality and 0.77 (n = 6; 95% CI: 0.71-0.83) for unfavorable functional outcomes. Subgroup analysis showed higher predictive performance for 6-month mortality (AUC = 0.81) and functional outcomes (AUC = 0.82) than for 12-month outcomes. The Helsinki score outperformed the Marshall (0.81 vs. 0.74) and Rotterdam (0.81 vs. 0.77) scores in predicting 6-month mortality and maintained robust performance for 12-month mortality (AUC = 0.75). Conclusion The Helsinki CT score suggests potential utility in predicting mortality and unfavorable functional outcomes in patients with TBI, particularly for short-term prognosis. Although the Helsinki score showed higher discriminatory power than the Marshall and Rotterdam scores in the available data, its performance may vary across clinical settings. It serves as an indicative adjunct for early risk stratification.

title: Nursing Ultrasound Monitoring of Arteriovenous Fistulas in Haemodialysis: The ECHO-NURSE Study.
abstract: Background Chronic kidney disease affects up to 16% of adults worldwide, and patients with kidney failure treated with haemodialysis require reliable vascular access. Autologous arteriovenous fistulas are the preferred access, yet their function may deteriorate due to stenosis or thrombosis. Doppler ultrasound is a key non‑invasive tool for assessing autologous arteriovenous fistula haemodynamics, but evidence on nurse‑performed serial Doppler monitoring remains limited, particularly in Italy. Objectives To describe temporal trends in Doppler-derived haemodynamic parameters measured by nurses and compare trajectories between patients with and without autologous arteriovenous fistula complications. Design Longitudinal observational study conducted over 4 months with monthly ultrasound assessments. Participants Forty‑two adults with a stable autologous arteriovenous fistula undergoing maintenance haemodialysis were enrolled; three presented with baseline stenosis. Measurements Nurses recorded brachial artery diameter, mean velocity, volumetric flow, end‑diastolic velocity, pulsatility index, and resistance index using standardised Doppler protocols. Linear mixed‑effects models evaluated level and trend differences between groups. Results Patients with stenosis showed consistently lower flow‑related parameters and higher Doppler indices. Vessel diameter and volumetric flow exhibited significantly attenuated temporal increases in the stenosis group (p < 0.001 for trend differences). Velocity parameters and Doppler indices displayed parallel trends but differed in mean levels. Conclusions Nurse‑performed serial Doppler monitoring characterised autologous arteriovenous fistula haemodynamics and distinguished profiles associated with stenosis. Findings support integrating structured ultrasound assessment into nursing‑led vascular access pathways.

title: Hepatic Steatosis in People With Chronic Hepatitis B in Africa: Prevalence, Correlates, and Clinical Significance.
abstract: To address data gaps around metabolic liver disease in Africa, within the Hepatitis B in Africa Collaborative Network (HEPSANET), we evaluated participants with chronic hepatitis B virus infection (CHB) for steatotic liver disease (SLD) using transient elastography with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). Using multivariable logistic regression, we identified sociodemographic, anthropometric, and clinical associations with SLD (CAP ≥ 248 dB/m), and evaluated whether SLD severity was independently associated with fibrosis. Short-term impacts of SLD on mortality were also assessed with Cox proportional hazards analysis. We also evaluated the diagnostic performance of B-mode ultrasound for SLD, with CAP as reference. Across 6 countries and 1601 participants (age range, 12-80 years; 39.5% female; 4% with diabetes; 11% unhealthy alcohol use; median body mass index, 24.4), 421 (26.3%) had SLD; 219 (13.7%) had severe steatosis (CAP ≥ 280 dB/m). Older age, male sex, overweight and obesity, and HIV-negative status were associated with SLD. After adjusting for age, sex, HIV status, HBV treatment, and country, severe steatosis, but not mild and moderate forms (i.e., 248-279 dB/m), was associated with a 8.4% (95%, 1.9%-14.9%) increased probability of fibrosis. Over limited follow-up (median 2.69 years) and small number of deaths, SLD was not associated with all-cause or liver-related mortality. B-mode ultrasound had low sensitivity for SLD, overall or when severe, but specificity was 95%. In conclusion, SLD was common in people with CHB in Africa and its severe form was associated with liver fibrosis. These data support screening for metabolic comorbidities as part of HBV care and treatment in Africa.

title: Application of Combined Gastric Tube Tip Manometry and Auscultation for Nasogastric Tube Positioning in Neurocritical Care Patients With Artificial Airways: A Prospective Diagnostic Pilot Study.
abstract: Background Nasogastric tube placement is central to enteral nutrition support in neurocritical care patients. However, tube malposition, particularly accidental placement into the airway, can lead to fatal complications. Aim To assess the accuracy of a combined gastric tube tip manometry and auscultation approach for confirming nasogastric tube placement in neurocritical care patients with artificial airways. Study design This prospective study enrolled patients who underwent nasogastric tube insertion in the neurocritical care unit of a tertiary hospital in China between January 2025 and May 2025. Using chest X-ray as the reference standard, we compared the sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), positive likelihood ratio (PLR) and negative likelihood ratio (NLR) for gastric tube tip manometry alone, auscultation alone and their combination. Results In total, 120 patients participated. X-ray confirmed correct nasogastric tube positioning in 119 patients and malposition in 1 patient. For gastric tube tip manometry alone, the sensitivity was 97.48%, with a specificity of 0%, a positive predictive value (PPV) of 99.15% and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 0%. Auscultation alone yielded a sensitivity of 90.76%, a specificity of 100%, a PPV of 100% and an NPV of 8.33%. The combined manometry-plus-auscultation approach had a sensitivity of 88.24%, a specificity of 100%, a PPV of 100% and an NPV of 6.67%. Conclusions The combined gastric tube tip manometry and auscultation method might serve as an adjunctive bedside strategy for confirming nasogastric tube placement in neurocritical care patients with artificial airways. However, only one malpositioned tube was observed in this study; the specificity and NPV should be interpreted with caution. Relevance to clinical practice When gastric aspirate cannot be obtained or immediate chest radiography is impractical, combined gastric tube tip manometry and auscultation provide a feasible, radiation-free bedside pathway for confirming nasogastric tube position; equivocal or negative bedside findings should still be verified radiographically before feeding. Trial registration The study was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2300078001).

title: Machine Learning Prediction of Orthodontic Extraction Patterns Using Multimodal Features Derived From Intraoral Scans and Lateral Cephalometric Radiographs.
abstract: Objective To develop and evaluate a machine learning framework for predicting orthodontic extraction patterns using features extracted from pretreatment intraoral scans (IOS) and lateral cephalometric radiographs (LCRs). Materials and methods This retrospective study included 420 subjects (mean age, 17.1 years; 61% female) with treatment plans involving dental extractions. Expert consensus-derived reference labels were established using a validated Delphi process involving four orthodontic experts. The dataset was randomly split into two mutually exclusive subsets: 30% for hyperparameter optimization using grid search with five-fold cross-validation and 70% (n = 294) for model development and evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV). Performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, likelihood ratios and F1 score. Results The Gradient Boosting classifier trained exclusively on canine-molar relationship features achieved the highest overall classification accuracy (79.9%), whereas the Random Forest multimodal model incorporating all IOS- and LCR-derived features achieved 78.2% accuracy and did not provide a significant improvement over canine-molar relationship features alone. SHAP analysis identified canine and molar relationships as the most influential predictors. For the Random Forest multimodal model, class-specific sensitivity (recall) was 84% for Class I, 77% for Class II, and 48% for Class III. Conclusions Sagittal canine-molar relationship features contained the greatest discriminative information for extraction pattern classification in this dataset, and incorporating the full multimodal feature set did not improve predictive performance. The substantially lower sensitivity for the underrepresented Class III pattern highlights the need for larger, more balanced datasets.

title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Associated Dry Mouth/Sicca Symptoms and Sjögren-Spectrum Toxicity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Reported Incidence.
abstract: Background This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the proportion of ICI-treated patients developing dry mouth/sicca symptoms, and to synthesize the evidence on clinical and serologic features of this condition. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were searched up to April 2026. Studies reporting data on sicca syndrome, xerostomia, sialadenitis, or Sjögren-spectrum toxicity in ICI-treated patients were included. Studies with an extractable denominator were included in the meta-analysis. Studies without a denominator were retained for descriptive synthesis. Risk-of-bias was assessed using the ROBINS-I tool for the denominator-based studies and the Joanna Briggs Institute checklists for case reports and case series. Results Twenty-three studies met eligibility criteria. Five studies (516 ICI-treated patients; 40 events) were included in the meta-analysis, giving an 8.7% (95% CI, 5.1%-14.3%) proportion of reported dry mouth/sicca symptoms of any severity, with moderate-to-substantial between-study heterogeneity (I 2 = 65.5%, 95% CI 9.9%-86.8%). Eighteen studies (83 patients) provided descriptive data on histopathology, serology, and latency. Conclusions ICI-associated dry mouth/sicca symptoms of any severity may occur in ICI-treated patients, presenting a clinical phenotype distinct from primary Sjögren's disease. The lack of symptoms assessment against Sjögren's disease classification criteria, salivary flow measurement, or biopsy in the pooled studies highlights the need for standardized, prospective studies incorporating objective diagnostic confirmation. Trial registration PROSPERO CRD420261371243.

title: Balancing Iliac Crest Avoidance and Neural Safety in L5/S1 TELD: Quantitative Identification of a Candidate Balanced Trajectory Window Using AI-Assisted 3D MRI Reconstruction.
abstract: Objective Transforaminal endoscopic lumbar discectomy (TELD) at L5/S1 is challenging due to the iliac crest barrier. Conventional planning relies on CT or 2D imaging, inherently lacking soft-tissue contrast to visualize neural structures. This study aimed to define a quantitative candidate balanced trajectory zone using AI-assisted 3D MRI reconstruction to simultaneously evaluate iliac crest obstruction and neural safety constraints. Methods A deep learning model was trained on 50 thin-slice lumbar MRIs to achieve precise segmentation and 3D reconstruction of neural, dural, and osseous structures. Thirty lumbar models were selected after image- and reconstruction-quality screening for surgical puncture simulation. Using a 5° increment as the angular increment, 49 virtual working trajectories (coronal plane angles, CPA 0°-30° and cross-sectional angles, CSA 0°-30°) were established for each bilateral intervertebral foramen, yielding a total of 2940 trajectories. Intersection volumes between each trajectory and the iliac crest, L5 nerve root, dural sac, and articular processes were quantitatively analyzed. Results The model achieved an 86.4% mean Dice coefficient (73.2%-92.4%). Among 2940 trajectories, 1207 (41.1%) completely avoided the iliac crest. Spatial analysis revealed a trade-off: increasing CSA reduced iliac and S1 superior articular process obstruction but increased L5 osseous removal, whereas steeper CPAs spared the L5 nerve root but risked the L5 inferior articular process. Quantitative analysis identified a candidate balanced trajectory window (CPA 20°-25°, CSA 25°-30°) that achieved a balance between iliac crest avoidance, neuro-osseous preservation, and facet integrity. Conclusions This candidate trajectory window (CPA 20°-25°/CSA 25°-30°) may provide a useful reference for balancing iliac crest avoidance with neuro-osseous safety. These findings provide quantitative constraints for manual planning and for the future development of computer-assisted trajectory-planning systems.

title: Association of Subscapularis Tear Severity With Posterosuperior Cuff Tear Morphology in a Combined-Tear Surgical Cohort: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Objectives In combined tears, the relationship between posterosuperior cuff tear (PSCT) morphology and subscapularis (SSC) tear severity is unknown. This study aimed to determine whether PSCT morphology is associated with SSC tear severity, which morphologies are associated with complete SSC rupture, and whether any association is confined to a particular severity threshold and persists after accounting for classification uncertainty and overall cuff extent. Methods A retrospective review of 368 patients who underwent arthroscopic surgery for combined, chronic, full-thickness PSCTs with concomitant SSC tears between 2016 and 2023 was conducted. High-resolution preoperative MRI and high-definition intraoperative video recordings were used to classify PSCT morphology (crescent, U-shaped, anterior L-shaped, posterior L-shaped, massive-retracted) and SSC tears (Lafosse Types I-V). Interobserver agreement was almost perfect for both classifications. Binary logistic regression (adjusted for age, sex, side, and BMI) was used to evaluate associations with complete subscapularis rupture (Lafosse IV/V). Results The mean patient age was 60.3 ± 9.2 years. PSCT morphology was significantly associated with SSC tear severity (Monte Carlo P less than 0.001; Cramer's V 0.234). The proportion with complete SSC rupture rose from 23.8% in posterior L-shaped and 25.6% in crescent tears to 39.6% in U-shaped, 60.9% in anterior L-shaped, and 71.4% in massive-retracted tears. Complete subscapularis rupture was significantly more likely in anterior L-shaped (adjusted OR 4.50, 95% CI 1.86 to 11.41) and massive-retracted morphologies (adjusted OR 7.12, 95% CI 2.24 to 27.17), both surviving correction (adjusted p = 0.003). Posterior L-shaped and U-shaped morphologies showed no significant difference from crescent tears. Conclusion In surgically treated combined tears, PSCT morphology shows a graded association with SSC tear severity that is concentrated in the anterior L-shaped and massive-retracted morphology patterns. However, because most complete ruptures overall occurred within crescent tears due to their high prevalence, morphology alone cannot serve as a definitive diagnostic rule-out tool. Nevertheless, anterior L-shaped or massive-retracted PSCT patterns warrant systematic inspection of the SSC.

Complete subscapularis rupture was significantly more likely in anterior L-shaped (adjusted OR 4.50, 95% CI 1.86 to 11.41) and massive-retracted morphologies (adjusted OR 7.12, 95% CI 2.24 to 27.17), both surviving correction (adjusted p = 0.003). Posterior L-shaped and U-shaped morphologies showed no significant difference from crescent tears.

Conclusion

In surgically treated combined tears, PSCT morphology shows a graded association with SSC tear severity that is concentrated in the anterior L-shaped and massive-retracted morphology patterns. However, because most complete ruptures overall occurred within crescent tears due to their high prevalence, morphology alone cannot serve as a definitive diagnostic rule-out tool. Nevertheless, anterior L-shaped or massive-retracted PSCT patterns warrant systematic inspection of the SSC.

title: The Clinical Outcome of a Fluoroscopy-Free "4-Step Cam Resection" Technique Compared With the Traditional Technique for Arthroscopic Treatment of Cam-Type Femoroacetabular Impingement.
abstract: Purpose To compare the clinical outcomes of the novel fluoroscopy-free "4-step cam resection" technique with the traditional cam resection method for treating cam-type FAI during hip arthroscopy. No established consensus exists on a standardized, reproducible technique that ensures complete cam resection without intraoperative fluoroscopy, and residual anterolateral cam deformity remains a leading cause of persistent impingement and revision surgery. The present study was therefore performed to determine whether the 4-step technique improves the completeness of cam resection compared with the conventional single-position technique. Methods Patients with symptomatic femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) who underwent the "4-step cam resection" technique between January 2021 and January 2022 were included. The 4-step intervention consisted of femoral head-neck osteoplasty performed sequentially with the hip placed in four positions: (i) 10° of flexion in maximal internal rotation; (ii) 10° of flexion in neutral rotation; (iii) 30° of flexion with rotation from internal to external; and (iv) 45° of flexion with rotation from internal to external. In the traditional technique, the cam lesion was resected with the hip in a single position of approximately 45° of flexion. No intraoperative fluoroscopy was used in either group. A historical control group extracted from our database was matched in a 1:1 ratio based on demographic and preoperative clinical variables. Outcomes were assessed using the Harris Hip Score (HHS), Hip Outcome Score (HOS), and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain. Radiographic measurements, including the lateral center-edge angle (LCEA) and alpha angle and gamma angle, were evaluated pre- and postoperatively. Results A total of 36 patients (36/40, 90.0%) in the study group (Group A, "4-step cam resection" technique) completed the final follow-up and 36 patients were matched as the control group (Group B, traditional technique). At a mean follow-up of 29 months, both groups demonstrated significant improvements in HOS, HHS, and VAS scores postoperatively (p < 0.05). Radiographic parameters including alpha angle, gamma angle, and LCEA were significantly reduced compared to preoperative values, with Group A showing significantly lower gamma angles and VAS for pain and a higher HOS-Sports score compared to Group B. The correlation analysis revealed that VAS (correlation coefficient = 0.281, p = 0.017) was correlated with gamma angle at the final follow-up. Conclusion The "4-step cam resection" technique achieves comparable subjective outcomes compared with the traditional technique and is associated with a greater decrease of gamma angle, lower VAS score, and better HOS-Sports outcome.

title: Application of Extraperitoneal Laparo-Endoscopic Single-Site Surgery in the Treatment of Lumbosacral Trunk Entrapment: A Cadaveric Study and Clinical Case Series.
abstract: Objective Management of pelvic fracture with lumbosacral trunk entrapment remains controversial. Open surgery (OS) carries significant technical challenges and risks. Our team innovatively proposed extraperitoneal laparo-endoscopic single-site surgery (ELESS) to explore and release the lumbosacral trunk. This study aimed to identify the key anatomical parameters of the lumbosacral trunk, to introduce ELESS techniques for exploration and release of lumbosacral trunk entrapment, and to evaluate its safety, feasibility, and clinical efficacy compared to OS. Methods This study measured lumbosacral trunk parameters in 12 cadavers, and retrospectively analyzed clinical data of 36 patients with lumbosacral trunk entrapment from May 2022 to September 2024. Combined with anatomical data, preoperative enhanced CT and MRN tests, the lumbosacral trunk decompression surgery was performed precisely via ELESS (n = 16) and OS (n = 20). Demographic, surgical technique details, and clinical outcomes were obtained from patient records. Independent samples t-tests, Mann-Whitney U test, or the Chi-square test were used to perform comparisons. Results The distance from the start of lumbosacral trunk to the sacroiliac joint was 14.85 ± 1.43 mm. The total length of the lumbosacral trunk was 34.95 ± 2.13 mm, and its width was 7.92 ± 1.11 mm. The patients were followed up for at least 16 months. The ELESS group demonstrated a significantly shorter operative time (131.5 ± 13.6 min) and reduced intraoperative blood loss (119.1 ± 28.1 mL) compared to the OS group (151.7 ± 27.9 min and 1010.5 ± 118.6 mL, p < 0.05). The incision visual analogue scale (VAS) scores in the ELESS group were lower than the OS group (p < 0.05). The muscle strength recovery rate was 88% in the ELESS group, showing no significant difference from the OS group (85%, p = 0.832). Sensory function recovery was observed in all patients. Conclusions Anatomical data is essential to identify and locate the lumbosacral trunk during surgery. The ELESS for lumbosacral trunk decompression offers the advantages of precision, minimal invasiveness, and safety. Compared to traditional OS, the ELESS is associated with less bleeding and shorter operative time, representing a reliable option for managing pelvic fractures with lumbosacral trunk entrapment.

title: Concurrent Long Thoracic and Lateral Cutaneous Intercostal Nerve Entrapment After Chest Tube Thoracostomy Causing Scapular Winging and Chest Wall Pain: Diagnosis With Ultrasound and Treatment With Hydrodissection.
abstract: Background Chest tube thoracostomy may cause iatrogenic nerve injury, resulting in persistent pain and functional impairment. Long thoracic nerve (LTN) palsy after chest tube placement has been described, but concurrent involvement of the LTN and the lateral cutaneous branch of an intercostal nerve (LCIN) appears to be rarely reported. We describe a patient with persistent post-thoracostomy chest wall pain and scapular winging in whom musculoskeletal ultrasonography identified entrapment of both nerves. Case presentation A 43-year-old man presented with severe left shoulder and chest wall pain 6 months after chest tube placement for traumatic hemopneumothorax. Examination demonstrated focal tenderness, dysesthesia, and mechanical allodynia at the chest tube scar, along with medial/inferior scapular winging during serratus anterior provocative testing. Shoulder range of motion was full on examination; however, forward flexion beyond 15° markedly aggravated pain, resulting in pain-related reluctance to move the shoulder. Manual muscle testing was 4+/5 before treatment because pain limited force generation. Musculoskeletal ultrasound demonstrated focal abnormality of the LTN where it pierced the axillary fascia over the sixth rib, with loss of fascicular definition and reduced glide, and tethering/thickening of the LCIN within scar tissue at the prior tube insertion site. Symptom reproduction with sonopalpation supported the clinical relevance of both findings. Intervention and results Ultrasound-guided hydrodissection using 5% dextrose in water was performed around both nerves. A total of approximately 40 mL of 5% dextrose in water was used, with 20 mL administered per nerve. Immediately after the first procedure, pain improved from NRS 9/10 to 2/10, with marked reduction in pain during shoulder movement, including forward flexion. The patient subsequently underwent 5 treatment sessions at 2-week intervals over 10 weeks. During follow-up, manual muscle testing improved to 5/5 without pain, scapular winging was no longer evident on provocative testing, and the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index improved from pain/disability scores of 25/15 to 6/4. At the sixth follow-up visit, pain and function were satisfactory, and the patient elected continued monitoring without further intervention. At 1-year follow-up, treatment efficacy remained sustained without recurrence. Conclusion In patients with persistent shoulder or chest wall pain after chest tube thoracostomy, iatrogenic peripheral nerve entrapment should be considered. This case highlights the value of a focused neuromuscular examination and musculoskeletal ultrasound for identifying concurrent motor and sensory nerve involvement and suggests that ultrasound-guided hydrodissection may be a useful minimally invasive treatment. Because electrodiagnostic studies were not performed, the findings are most consistent with entrapment/neurapraxia with dynamic tethering rather than electrodiagnostically proven axonal palsy.

title: Pediatric Kidney Transplantation in the Setting of Inferior Vena Cava Thrombosis or Atresia: A Single-Center Case Series and Considerations for Operative Planning.
abstract: Background Chronic occlusion of the IVC poses a major technical challenge in pediatric kidney transplantation, since standard implantation depends on reliable iliac or caval venous drainage. When this pathway is compromised, transplant teams must identify alternative outflow routes while minimizing ischemia time and graft thrombosis risk. Pediatric-specific guidance remains limited to single-case reports rather than systematic preoperative planning. Methods We conducted a single-center, retrospective review of three kidney transplants in two pediatric patients with IVC occlusion at Texas Children's Hospital (2018-2026). Records were reviewed for demographics, operative details, and short-term outcomes. Operative notes were assessed for surgical approach, intraoperative findings, and technical modifications. Available imaging (Doppler ultrasound, CT angiography, MRI/MRA, direct venography) was re-evaluated for thrombus extent, collateral anatomy, and outflow patency. Results The first patient had congenital IVC hypoplasia and underwent deceased donor transplantation complicated by intraoperative venous outflow obstruction; the graft was explanted, flushed, and reimplanted using a donor iliac vein conduit to the superior mesenteric/portal system. Eight years later, the same patient underwent re-transplantation via the external iliac vein after imaging confirmed adequate collateral drainage. The second patient, with chronic IVC thrombosis after VA-ECMO, underwent living donor transplantation using a patent segment of infrarenal IVC and aorta. All three transplants achieved excellent short-term allograft function. Conclusion IVC occlusion should not be considered an absolute contraindication to pediatric kidney transplantation. Success depends on dedicated preoperative vascular imaging, multidisciplinary review, identification of feasible outflow targets, and intraoperative readiness to adapt to the operative plan.

title: Do Interindividual Differences Matter? Testing Differences in Locus Coeruleus MRI Contrast as a Function of Age, Sex, and Body Mass Index.
abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC) plays a key role in cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease (AD). Investigating demographic differences in the LC is important because these differences may contribute to lifelong AD risk. Noninvasive MRI assessments of LC contrast are associated with cognitive performance and are hypothesized to reflect the nucleus's structural integrity. Age and sex differences in LC MRI contrast have been documented. Nonetheless, results are mixed, and most previous studies are hampered by small samples and a lack of standardization in the inspection of data quality and registration accuracy. In this cross-sectional study, we aim to investigate differences in LC MRI contrast as a function of demographic variables associated with increased AD prevalence: age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). We will pool fast spin echo (FSE) scans of young (age: 18-33) and older adults (age: 55-90) from eight datasets collected in three sites (N = 663). A semiautomatic pipeline will be adopted to register FSE scans to MNI space and segment the LC using a high-confidence LC mask. To maximize reproducibility, we will evaluate data quality using markers of in-scanner motion and nonphysiological noise, and we will rely on a standardized visual inspection to assess registration accuracy. We will run linear mixed models, including a nested random effect of acquisition batch (i.e., datasets grouped by study and site) to account for variability in LC MRI contrast driven by non-biological factors (e.g., hardware). We expect that LC contrast is positively associated with chronological age in young adults but negatively associated in older adults. On average, it is expected to be higher in older adults and in females. We will explore sex-by-age-group effects and BMI differences in LC MRI contrast. This study offers a reproducible foundation for understanding demographic variation in LC MRI contrast.

title: Detection of Urinary Round Cells in a Dog With IgA Paraproteinemia: A Case of Myeloma-Related Disorder.
abstract: An 11-year-old neutered male Rottweiler mixed-breed dog was presented with apathy, anorexia, and polyuria/polydipsia. Clinicopathologic evaluation revealed hypercalcemia, azotemia, mild hyperproteinemia, and hyperglobulinemia, and proteinuria with concurrent glucosuria. Urinary cytology identified numerous neoplastic round cells morphologically consistent with plasma cells. Abdominal ultrasound demonstrated hepatic and splenic hypoechoic lesions, lymphadenomegaly, and hypoechoic prostatic parenchyma. Cytology of aspirates from hepatic and splenic lesions revealed the same neoplastic round cell population as observed in the urine. Based on these findings, a presumptive diagnosis of myeloma-related disorder (MRD), most likely multiple myeloma (MM), was made. Further laboratory investigations were pursued with serum protein electrophoresis (SPE) and immunofixation (IM), as well as immunocytochemistry. SPE coupled with IM revealed an IgA paraproteinemia, and immunocytochemistry findings were suggestive of plasma cell differentiation. The present findings are indicative of an MRD. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first description of plasmacytoid cells in urine from a dog with concurrent paraproteinemia, highlighting urine cytology as a potential non-invasive diagnostic tool for MRD.

title: Retrospective Description of the Outcomes of Dogs With Intraperitoneal Dissemination of Bladder Uroliths and Septic Uroabdomen: Eight Cases From Four Hospitals (2014-2024).
abstract: Objectives To describe the clinical features, diagnosis, treatment, and prognosis for dogs diagnosed with septic uroabdomen secondary to bladder rupture and dissemination of uroliths in the peritoneal cavity. Design Retrospective study. Setting Two veterinary teaching hospitals and two private referral hospitals. Animals Eight adult client-owned dogs. Measurements and main results Bladder rupture and migration of uroliths in the abdomen were observed intraoperatively in all eight dogs. Free abdominal uroliths were detected preoperatively by abdominal ultrasonography in three of eight dogs and by radiography in two of five dogs. Partial cystectomy due to bladder wall necrosis was performed in seven of eight dogs. Cytology of the peritoneal fluid identified bacteria in all dogs, and positive culture results were available in seven of eight. The most commonly reported bacterium was Staphylococcus spp. in five of seven dogs, and only one multidrug-resistant bacterial species was isolated. Struvite was the most common type of urolith. No intraoperative or long-term postoperative complications were reported, and all dogs survived to hospital discharge. Mild, transient incontinence occurred in two dogs. Conclusions Septic uroabdomen secondary to bladder rupture and dissemination of uroliths in the peritoneal cavity can result in a good to excellent prognosis. Because uroliths may not always be detectable on preoperative imaging, a thorough abdominal exploration is recommended.

title: Meibomian Gland Epithelioma Mimicking Eyelid Squamous Cell Carcinoma in a Hereford-Cross Steer.
abstract: Objective To describe the clinical presentation and histopathology of a meibomian gland epithelioma that clinically resembled squamous cell carcinoma in a steer. Animal studied A 15 year-old Hereford-Lowline cross steer presented for evaluation of an approximately 2 × 4 cm ulcerated, pedunculated eyelid mass arising from the right inferior eyelid margin. Procedures Excision of the mass followed by adjunctive cryotherapy was performed. The mass was submitted for histopathologic analysis. Results Histopathologic evaluation revealed the mass to be consistent with a meibomian gland epithelioma, a neoplastic proliferation of the basal/reserve cells of the meibomian gland. The steer recovered routinely from the procedure with no evidence of regrowth of the mass at 13 months post-operatively. Conclusion Meibomian gland epitheliomas are one of the most common eyelid tumors of dogs; however, this is the first known report of a histologically confirmed meibomian gland epithelioma in cattle. Clinically, the mass resembled the appearance of squamous cell carcinoma, a common eyelid tumor in Hereford cattle. The clinical misclassification of a benign eyelid mass as squamous cell carcinoma could lead to unnecessary aggressive management such as enucleation, exenteration, or culling. This case confirms the importance of histopathologic analysis of excised tissues to reach an accurate diagnosis and appropriate treatment and follow-up plans.
