title: Idiopathic Granulomatous Inflammation of the Periocular Structures in Four Dogs: Clinical, Histopathological, and Imaging Findings and Therapeutic Outcome.
abstract: Purpose To describe cases of canine idiopathic periocular granulomatous inflammation. Material and methods Clinical records were reviewed. Animal studied At the time of presentation, the four patients (German Shepherd dog, mixed breed, Magyar Vizsla, Hovawart) were 1.5-5 (mean 3.75) years old. All dogs were female; two were spayed. Lesions were unilateral in 3/4 cases. Dogs presented with ulcerated (1) or non-ulcerated (3) mass lesions affecting the periocular skin (3/4), medial canthal area (2/4), or third eyelid (1/4). Results Incisional biopsies revealed pyogranulomatous inflammation in three and granulomatous inflammation in one case. There was no evidence of microbial infection in the specimens. Patients received anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressive dosages of systemic corticosteroids. Three dogs also received systemic cyclosporin (5 mg/kg, sid), and one dog received topical cyclosporin (0.1%, bid). One dog underwent surgical debulking of a circumscribed mass within the left lower eyelid prior to immunosuppressive therapy and developed an additional swelling on the left upper eyelid. Remission of clinical signs was achieved in all patients. Dogs were treated for 5 to 11 months (mean 8.7). No recurrence was reported in 4/4 patients during a mean follow-up period of 17.3 months. In 3/4patients, there was no recurrence within an average of 11 months after discontinuation of therapy. One dog was lost to follow-up. Conclusion Idiopathic granulomatous inflammation is a differential diagnosis for periocular mass lesions. Its diagnosis is based on histopathology and the exclusion of other causes of granulomatous inflammation.

title: Computed Tomographic Findings of Hepatic Rupture Associated With Amyloidosis in a Young Siamese Cat.
abstract: A 3-year-old neutered male Siamese cat with chronic anorexia showed anemia and elevated liver enzyme levels. Ultrasonography disclosed multiple diffusely heterogeneous hepatic lesions and peritoneal effusion, which was identified as hemoabdomen upon fluid analysis. Computed tomography showed finger-like hypoattenuation extending from the left hepatic margin with focal margin loss in the delayed phase, suggesting hepatic rupture. Infiltrative hepatic diseases were considered, and amyloidosis was the top differential diagnosis given the patient's young age, breed predisposition, and suspected hepatic rupture. Blood oozing was confirmed via laparotomy, and Congo red staining established hepatic amyloidosis, though amyloid typing was not pursued.

title: Radiographic Comparison of Pulmonary Lobar Vasculature Dimensions in Medically Managed and Drug-Naive Dogs With Left Heart Failure Secondary to Myxomatous Mitral Valve Disease.
abstract: Myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) is the most common acquired cause of left heart failure (LHF) in dogs, and radiographic identification of pulmonary venous enlargement is traditionally used to support the diagnosis of LHF. However, the absence of venous enlargement has been anecdotally observed after initiation of therapy. Therefore, we aimed to compare radiographic pulmonary vessel size in LHF patients with ongoing medical management ± receiving acute rescue therapy. Dogs with echocardiographically confirmed MMVD and radiographic cardiogenic pulmonary edema were retrospectively selected. Pulmonary lobar artery and vein widths were measured using standardized rib-to-vessel ratios: cranial vessels at the intersection with the fourth rib on lateral projections and caudal vessels at the ninth rib on ventrodorsal/dorsoventral projections. Pulmonary vein-to-artery (PV/PA) and vessel-to-rib ratios were calculated, with enlargement defined as >1.2 and small vessel size as <0.8, and treatment groups were compared using Welch-corrected t-tests. 200 radiographic studies from 163 dogs were reviewed. In all dogs, the veins measured larger than the arteries in all lung lobes. Chronically untreated dogs who received furosemide immediately before radiographs had no venous enlargement. All other groups had vascular asymmetry or venous enlargement in at least two lung lobes. All control dogs with reoccurrence of LHF had absence of venous enlargement after initiation of therapy. Pulmonary venous enlargement was most pronounced in the right caudal lung lobe. These findings indicate that dogs chronically managed for MMVD may decompensate into LHF without radiographic pulmonary venous enlargement and that furosemide administration prior to imaging can normalize vessel size.

title: Computed Tomographic Findings of Ischemic Necrosis of the Accessory Carpal Bone in a Dog.
abstract: A 1-year-and-9-month-old Golden Retriever presented with a 9-month history of right thoracic limb lameness. Radiographs revealed a monostotic, expansile lesion of the right accessory carpal bone (ACB). A computed tomography (CT) confirmed the aggressive nature of the lesion, demonstrating multifocal moth-eaten osteolysis, sclerosis, periosteal reaction, and flexor carpi ulnaris tendinopathy. Differential diagnoses included the ischemic necrosis of the ACB, osteomyelitis, and primary bone neoplasia. Histopathology confirmed osteonecrosis. This case highlights the value of CT in evaluating aggressive carpal lesions and identifies ischemic necrosis as an important differential diagnosis. This case represents the first CT description of this disease in dogs.

title: Evaluation of Intracranial Lesions Using Deep Learning-Based Reconstruction in Canine Brain MRI: Comparison With Conventional Reconstruction on T2-Weighted and FLAIR Sequences.
abstract: Obtaining high-resolution brain MRI in small animals is challenging due to the inherent trade-off between image quality and acquisition time. Deep learning-based reconstruction (DLR) has emerged as a solution to improve image quality without prolonging scan time; however, its clinical utility and potential risks, such as pseudolesions, remain insufficiently evaluated in veterinary patients. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of DLR on lesion assessment and image quality in canine brain MRI and to investigate potential limitations associated with its application. This retrospective study compared DLR with conventional reconstruction in 25 canine brain MRI examinations diagnosed with intracranial diseases. Transverse T2-weighted and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery sequences were reconstructed using both conventional and DLR methods. Quantitative analysis included signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and lesion edge sharpness. Two blinded radiologists assessed image quality, lesion conspicuity, artifacts, pseudolesions, and lesion masking. DLR images exhibited significantly higher SNR, CNR, and lesion edge sharpness than conventional images in both sequences (p < 0.05). DLR images also yielded significantly higher qualitative scores for image quality and lesion conspicuity (p < 0.05). Truncation artifact was significantly reduced, whereas motion and pulsation artifacts showed no improvement. No instances of pseudolesions or lesion masking were noted. DLR significantly improves image quality and lesion conspicuity in canine brain MRI and reduces truncation artifacts; however, it does not mitigate motion or pulsation interference. Collectively, these findings suggest that DLR has potential value for improving image quality and lesion visibility in canine brain MRI, whereas further studies are needed to determine its impact on diagnostic performance.

title: Intraoperative Extracorporeal Irradiation of Craniotomy Bone Flap for Skull Reconstruction Following Brain Meningioma Resection in a Cat.
abstract: A 6-year-old male neutered domestic shorthair cat underwent rostro-tentorial biparietal craniotomy for meningioma resection. The bone flap was removed under sterile conditions and subjected to extracorporeal irradiation with 100 Gy before reimplantation using nonabsorbable sutures. Postoperative MRI confirmed gross total resection of the mass. Seven-month follow-up with CT showed no evidence of tumor recurrence and successful integration of the bone flap. To our knowledge, this is the first report of intraoperative extracorporeal irradiation of a craniotomy flap in veterinary medicine and suggests its potential as a viable alternative for skull reconstruction.

title: Accuracy of intraoperative gross margin assessment by veterinary surgeons compared with histologic margin evaluation: A multicenter prospective cohort study.
abstract: Objective To identify the sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and accuracy of intraoperative surgeon-perceived margin status via gross examination compared to histologic evaluation for marginal and wide cutaneous mass excisions. Study design Multicenter prospective cohort study. Animal population A total of 84 dogs and six cats with 102 cutaneous masses. Methods Four surgeons completed a survey assessing margin completeness after mass removal prior to histologic results. Results Surgeon ability to identify incomplete margins had a sensitivity of 56.3%, specificity of 87.2%, PPV of 45%, NPV of 91.5%, and accuracy of 82.4%. Surgeon margin assessment was correct in 58.5% of marginally excised and 98.4% of widely excised masses: odds ratio (OR) 0.024 (confidence interval [CI]: 0.003, 0.19). Margin assessment based upon cytologic malignancy status was correct in nine of 14 (64.3%) benign lesions and 75 of 88 (85.2%) malignant lesions: OR 0.31 (CI: 0.09, 1.1). Conclusion Surgeons did not have improved accuracy in margin assessment for cytologically benign masses compared with malignant masses. Surgeon margin assessment correctness may be influenced by surgical dose. Additionally, when surgeons suspected a complete margin, there was a high probability that the histologic margin was complete. Limitations included the diversity of cases enrolled, few participating surgeons, potential non-blinded assessment bias, and lack of clinical follow up. Clinical significance Veterinary surgeons can provide owners an assessment of margin completeness with a degree of confidence for wide mass excision. Caution should persist in assessment of marginally excised tumors. This information allows owners to contemplate further treatment pending histopathology results.

title: Do canine elbow arthroplasty implants demonstrate morphological conformity for use in companion pigs with osteoarthritis?
abstract: To identify whether the largest commercially available canine cementless total elbow arthroplasty system (TATE size 19 mm) demonstrates morphological conformity with the elbows of companion miniature pig elbows with osteoarthritis (OA). Retrospective, cross-sectional, comparative morphometric study. Computed tomography (CT) scans from university veterinary hospitals were retrospectively evaluated in groups according to the presence or absence of OA. Companion pig elbows without OA (n = 75) and with OA (n = 78). Humeral and radial medial-lateral articular widths were measured from CT images. Three-dimensional models were subsequently generated by segmentation and used to quantify the resurfacing depth and radius of curvature (RoC) of the medial and lateral aspects of the humeral and radial condyles. The presence of OA was associated with the humerus RoC (F = 51.9, partial η2 = 0.151, p-value = <0.001). The estimated OA humeral RoC mean was 14.2 mm (95% CI: 9.80-18.7 mm), partially exceeding the implant's humeral component RoC. There was no OA, weight, or age effect on the radius RoC measures. The estimated OA radius RoC mean was 17.8 mm (95% CI=11.9-52.8 mm). OA was also associated with the humerus (F = 20.6, partial η2 = 0.125, p-value = <0.001) and radius (F = 23.7, partial η2 = 0.142, p-value = <0.001) resurface depths. The estimated mean for the OA humerus and radius resurface depths were 4.9 mm (95% CI 95%: 2.7-7.1 mm) and 4.8 mm (95% CI: 2.4-7.2 mm), respectively. This measure includes resurface depths beyond the theoretical 4 mm resurface depth for each bone. Lastly, there was no association with OA to humerus and radius medio-lateral width, but both estimated means were larger than the medio-lateral width of the corresponding implant components. The differences in the humerus and radius condyle medio-lateral width, resurface depth and RoC in pigs with OA compared to the canine implant width suggests that a novel pig elbow implant would potentially benefit elbow arthroplasty in this species. The difference in morphology and conformity between the available implant and elbows of a large population of companion pigs suggests the potential need for a porcine-specific elbow implant for companion pigs with elbow OA refractory to medical management.

title: Intrametatarsal pad injection of indocyanine green for near-infrared fluorescence imaging of the thoracic duct in four dogs and two cats with chylothorax.
abstract: Objective To assess the efficacy of direct near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) using indocyanine green (ICG) via intrametatarsal pad injection in dogs and cats with idiopathic chylothorax. Study design Retrospective case series of client-owned animals undergoing intrametatarsal ICG injection and thoracoscopic thoracic duct ligation between 2020 and 2025. Animals A total of four dogs and two cats. Methods Inclusion criteria consisted of cytologically confirmed chylothorax, preoperative computed tomography (CT) lymphangiogram (CTL), and known intraoperative injection of ICG in the metatarsal pad(s). Data collected included signalment, weight, preoperative diagnostics, number of ducts visualized intraoperatively, dose of ICG, additional doses required, and concordance with CTL. Time to visualization of the ICG in the thoracic duct, surgical procedures performed, and any intraoperative complications encountered were also reported. Postoperative data included time to discharge, time to first recheck, presence of fluid at first recheck, postoperative complications, status at last recheck, and total follow-up time. Results Median number of ducts seen between T10 and 13 region on preoperative CT was 2.5 (range: 1-4). The ICG dose ranged from 0.06 to 0.25 mg/kg, and two cases required additional injections to visualize the duct and all branches. A duct not previously seen on CT was visualized with NIRF in one dog. Median time to TD visualization was 7 min (range: 5-22 min). No intra- or postoperative complications due to the metatarsal injections were reported, and all patients were discharged. A total of 5/6 patients did not require thoracocentesis and were clinically well at a median last follow-up of 647 days (range: 454-793). Conclusion Intrametatarsal injection of ICG appears effective for identification of the thoracic duct in animals with chylothorax.

title: Development and preliminary in silico and three-dimensional model assessment of a feline universal sacroiliac guide (FUSIG): An exploratory morphometric study.
abstract: To characterize feline sacral morphometry and to develop and perform a preliminary internal assessment of a feline universal sacroiliac guide (FUSIG) intended to assist screw placement within the feline sacral safe corridor. Retrospective, exploratory morphometric study with in silico and three-dimensional (3D)-printed model assessment. A total of 34 client-owned cats. Computed tomography studies of the sacrum were segmented, and multiplanar morphometric analysis identified a corridor-derived geometric reference point (B) at the center of the predefined sacral safe corridor. Linear distances of the sacral articular surface and angular inclinations were measured. A population-based guide was subsequently designed, mirrored for laterality, and assessed virtually using a simulated 2.7-mm screw path. Physical assessment used 3D-printed sacra and guides. The primary outcome was the proportion of screw paths fully contained within the sacral safe corridor; secondary outcomes were the direction of cortical breach and descriptive morphometric variability. A total of 61 hemisacra were analyzed. Sacral articular surface width and length were 12.9 ± 0.6 mm and 14.1 ± 0.7 mm, respectively, with a safe-corridor length of 23.6 ± 1.8 mm. Linear measurements showed low interindividual variability (%CV 4.9%-7.8%). Mean dorsoventral and craniocaudal inclinations were 19.0 ± 2.2° and 20.1 ± 2.4°. In silico and 3D-model assessment each achieved 98% screw containment, with one minor deviation per phase. Feline sacral morphometry showed relatively low variability across this study population, supporting the development of a single population-based guide. Under idealized conditions, the FUSIG produced screw trajectories contained within the sacral corridor in in silico simulations and 3D-printed feline sacral models. The FUSIG may represent a reusable, anatomy-driven method for accurate sacroiliac stabilization in cats. Cadaveric studies are required before clinical application.

title: Diagnostic Utility of Serial Radiography in Foot Osteomyelitis in People With Diabetes: Influence of Operator Experience on Test Performance.
abstract: Plain radiography is first-line imaging for suspected osteomyelitis in persons with diabetes (DFO); however, its sensitivity in early disease is limited. Serial radiography may improve detection and inform prognosis, yet its utility remains uncertain. We performed a retrospective multi-reader diagnostic accuracy study in the BeBoP cohort of persons with diabetes and clinically suspected DFO who underwent percutaneous bone biopsy. Cases with baseline (T0) and ~6-week follow-up (T1) foot radiographs were included. Four readers (two radiologists and two non-radiologists) rated DFO probability on a 5-point scale at T0, T1, and serial (T0 + T1). Histopathology and/or culture of percutaneous bone biopsy defined DFO. Discrimination across conditions was evaluated using ROC analysis, DeLong's test. Mixed-effects models evaluated correct classification and diagnostic ratings. Thirty-four cases were included; 27/34 (79.4%) had DFO. Multi-reader AUCs were 0.52 (T0), 0.64 (T1), and 0.65 (serial) with no significant differences between AUC for serial versus T1. Mixed-effects models showed higher odds of correct classification for serial versus T0 conditions. Radiologists outperformed non-radiologists at T0, but not serial readings; interrater agreement was moderate (κ = 0.44). Reader experience was not associated with AUC. Serial radiography modestly improved accuracy over baseline but did not perform better than single follow-up imaging, and reader experience did not influence performance. Serial radiography should be considered supportive in the multidisciplinary evaluation of suspected DFO.

title: Metabolic and structural profiling of phosphaturic mesenchymal tumors by multimodal optical spectroscopy: a case study.
abstract: Significance Optical spectroscopy-based imaging is not commonly used for the diagnosis of phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor (PMT), which are rare neoplasms often associated with tumor-induced osteomalacia. Accurate diagnosis of PMT is clinically challenging due to their small size, variable localization, and nonspecific presentation and usually relies on a combination of clinical and laboratory data, as well as functional and anatomical imaging techniques. Aim Optical spectroscopic methods are of great interest for analyzing the metabolism and growth characteristics of tumor and stromal cells, as well as extracellular matrix components, which may provide complementary diagnostic information. Approach We present an ex vivo analysis of surgically removed PMT samples obtained from two patients. Results Comprehensive spectroscopic characterization was performed, including autofluorescence, diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) in the visible range, Raman spectroscopy, and fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM). Cell cultures obtained from PMT of one patient were also analyzed. Conclusions The obtained results demonstrate the potential utility of multimodal optical spectroscopy for intraoperative PMT delineation and suggest its applicability in distinguishing PMT subtypes based on their biochemical and metabolic profiles.

title: Noise2Flow: single-image conditional mean denoising flows from weak-anchor couplings.
abstract: Purpose Single-image denoising is needed when clean targets and repeated acquisitions are unavailable, as in low-dose computed tomography (CT) and fluorescence microscopy. Existing per-image methods often assume pixel-wise noise independence, which fails under spatially correlated noise, and imperfect single-image denoisers commonly leave residual noise. We learn a proxy mean-velocity direction field from one noisy image so that a single transport step exceeds the imperfect anchors used as supervision. Approach Noise2Flow runs weak single-image denoisers on the noisy image to form source-target couplings. The displacement from input to anchor is a directional proxy for the mean restoration velocity. For each imposed linear segment, MeanFlow's finite-interval average velocity reduces exactly to a constant secant. A flow network is trained with a direction-normalized objective that regularizes predictions at states in a stochastic tube around the noisy-to-anchor segment toward a common secant direction. At inference, the weak denoisers are discarded; one update with a calibrated transport budget restores the image. Results On the fluorescence microscopy denoising (FMD) test set of 48 images, Noise2Flow reaches 34.91 dB peak signal-to-noise ratio and 0.887 structural similarity, 0.52 dB above Filter2Noise, and 1.00 dB above Noise2Detail. On 1311 low-dose CT slices from 10 Mayo Clinic patients, it reaches 28.82 dB and 0.714, 0.91 dB above Filter2Noise and 1.23 dB above Noise2Detail. One-step inference is within 0.11 dB of 10-step Heun; tube sampling improves the 10-step Heun result relative to on-segment training; a calibrated extrapolation factor moves the flow past residual-noise anchors of varying quality. Conclusions A proxy mean-velocity direction field can be learned from a single noisy medical image by treating weak-denoiser outputs as directional anchors rather than final targets. The straight proxy path defines the one-step endpoint update; tube regularization and calibrated extrapolation carry that update past residual-noise anchors. The learned flow exceeds residual-noise anchors and supports reference-free restoration in data-limited imaging.

title: Representation geometry and task performance in vision-language modeling for computed tomography enterography.
abstract: Purpose Computed tomography (CT) enterography is central to inflammatory bowel disease evaluation, but optimal representation choices for vision-language learning on this volumetric modality are unclear. We establish baseline performance and quantify how aggregation, slice encoding, and retrieval context affect classification, retrieval, and report generation. Approach We fine-tuned vision-language models on abdominal CT enterography with parameter-efficient adapters and compared (i) mean versus attention pooling of slice embeddings, (ii) multiwindow red-green-blue Hounsfield-unit encoding versus multiplanar sampling for added spatial coverage, and (iii) report generation with versus without retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). A three-teacher pseudolabel framework enabled evaluation without expert annotations. Classification and retrieval comparisons used three training seeds. Results Mean and attention pooling achieved the same mean three-class disease classification accuracy (55.7%; standard deviations of 2.0 and 2.4 percentage points) at the largest low-rank adaptation capacity. Neither consistently outperformed the other at matched capacity with central sampling. Sixteen slices at 20% to 80% had higher classification accuracy than 8 slices, 32 slices, and 10% to 90% sampling in all three seeds for both pooling methods. The tested multiplanar configurations had lower classification accuracy. For report generation, fine-tuning without retrieval performed at prevalence-matched chance for within-1 report-label agreement (70.4% versus 71.0% random). RAG improved within-1 report-label agreement by 7 to 14 points over chance and reduced ordinal mean absolute error from 0.98 to 0.80-0.89. Conclusions Slice sampling and tissue-contrast-focused encoding affect performance in CT enterography vision-language systems, and RAG improved report-label agreement over the fine-tuned baseline. These results provide initial baselines and practical guidance for multimodal learning in volumetric CT.

We fine-tuned vision-language models on abdominal CT enterography with parameter-efficient adapters and compared (i) mean versus attention pooling of slice embeddings, (ii) multiwindow red-green-blue Hounsfield-unit encoding versus multiplanar sampling for added spatial coverage, and (iii) report generation with versus without retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). A three-teacher pseudolabel framework enabled evaluation without expert annotations. Classification and retrieval comparisons used three training seeds.

Results

Mean and attention pooling achieved the same mean three-class disease classification accuracy (55.7%; standard deviations of 2.0 and 2.4 percentage points) at the largest low-rank adaptation capacity. Neither consistently outperformed the other at matched capacity with central sampling. Sixteen slices at 20% to 80% had higher classification accuracy than 8 slices, 32 slices, and 10% to 90% sampling in all three seeds for both pooling methods. The tested multiplanar configurations had lower classification accuracy. For report generation, fine-tuning without retrieval performed at prevalence-matched chance for within-1 report-label agreement (70.4% versus 71.0% random). RAG improved within-1 report-label agreement by 7 to 14 points over chance and reduced ordinal mean absolute error from 0.98 to 0.80-0.89.

Conclusions

Slice sampling and tissue-contrast-focused encoding affect performance in CT enterography vision-language systems, and RAG improved report-label agreement over the fine-tuned baseline. These results provide initial baselines and practical guidance for multimodal learning in volumetric CT.

title: Evaluating GPT-5 as a generalist multimodal clinical model.
abstract: Purpose The transition from task-specific artificial intelligence toward general-purpose foundation models raises fundamental questions about their capacity to support the integrated reasoning required in clinical medicine, where diagnosis demands synthesis of ambiguous patient narratives, laboratory data, and multimodal imaging. Approach We provide the first controlled, cross-sectional evaluation of the GPT-5 family (GPT-5, GPT-5 Mini, and GPT-5nano) against its predecessor GPT-4o across a diverse spectrum of clinically grounded tasks, grounded tasks, including the United States Medical Licensing Examination, text-based, text-based reasoning benchmarks (MedQA and MedXpertQA Text), and visual question answering (VQA) in neuroradiology (BraTS), digital pathology (PathVQA and BreakHis), and mammography (EMBED, InBreast, Chinese Mammography Database, and CBIS-DDSM) using a standardized zero-shot chain-of-thought protocol. Results GPT-5 demonstrated substantial performance gains with absolute improvements exceeding 25 percentage points on MedXpertQA. When tasked with multimodal synthesis, GPT-5 effectively leveraged its enhanced training corpora to achieve state-of-the-art or competitive performance across most VQA benchmarks and outperformed GPT-4o by margins of 10% to 40% in mammography tasks requiring fine-grained lesion characterization. However, performance remained moderate in neuroradiology (44% macro-average accuracy) and lagged substantially behind domain-specific models in mammography, where specialized systems exceed 80% accuracy compared with GPT-5's 52% to 64%. Conclusions These findings indicate that although GPT-5 represents a meaningful advance toward general, multimodal clinical inference, generalist models are still not yet substitutes for purpose-built systems in highly specialized, perception-critical tasks. We delineate the current VQA landscape, positioning GPT-5 as a powerful adjunct capable of holistic inference while underscoring that domain adaptation, rigorous validation, and guarantees of reasoning transparency remain essential prerequisites for clinical deployment.

title: Pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of early lupus nephritis via a 68 Ga-labeled single-stranded DNA probe.
abstract: As a major cause of morbidity in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), the prognosis of lupus nephritis (LN) critically depends on early detection and timely intervention. However, current diagnostic approaches remain suboptimal: renal biopsy is invasive and unsuitable for longitudinal monitoring, while conventional urine tests lack sensitivity for early-stage disease. Here, we report a molecular imaging strategy designed to target the pathogenic DNA-anti-dsDNA antibody axis for non-invasive detection of LN. We engineered a gallium-68-labeled single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) probe ([ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA) and evaluated its diagnostic performance and biosafety in the spontaneous MRL/lpr lupus mouse model. The probe showed disease-associated and sustained renal accumulation in 16-week-old diseased MRL/lpr mice, with progressively increasing kidney-to-background contrast. More importantly, [ 68 Ga]Ga-NOTA-ssDNA enabled detection of renal immune complex deposition as early as 10 weeks of age, preceding abnormalities in conventional renal function markers and positive findings in renal histology by approximately two weeks. Mechanistically, the ssDNA backbone demonstrated favorable biocompatibility, without exacerbating autoimmune phenotypes or inducing Toll-like receptor-mediated signaling pathways. In conclusion, this study establishes a robust proof-of-concept for pathology-targeted PET/CT imaging of immune complex deposition. By directly visualizing the disease-driving renal autoantibody deposition at the preclinical stage, prior to overt organ damage, this strategy shifts LN diagnosis to non-invasive, mechanism-based molecular visualization.

title: Human carotid plaque risk imaging using multiparametric photoacoustic and ultrasound fusion (hCAPRI).
abstract: Assessing the risk of carotid plaque rupture remains limited because current imaging methods cannot provide both plaque composition and structural information in real time. Here, we present human carotid plaque risk imaging (hCAPRI), a multiparametric photoacoustic and ultrasound (PA/US) fusion method for real-time carotid plaque assessment. hCAPRI combines PA imaging for detecting intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) with US imaging for evaluating the plaque structure. PA imaging measured IPH size and methemoglobin content, while US imaging assessed stenosis severity, calcification, and plaque thickness. Combining these PA/US parameters, we compute an hCAPRI score. In 171 carotid arteries (CAs) from 120 patients, hCAPRI revealed the relationships among the PA/US parameters. In 36 CAs validated with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), hCAPRI showed high agreement with MRI. The hCAPRI score achieved 89% sensitivity and 84% specificity for high-risk plaque classification. hCAPRI offers a low-cost, real-time, and contrast-free approach for carotid plaque risk imaging.

title: Lighting up necrotic neurons from traumatic brain injury with magnetic quantum dots to decode the cellular origin of MRI.
abstract: The diagnosis of traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains heavily constrained by the limitations of conventional imaging techniques in visualizing the pathological events that determine the disease progression and outcome. To address this clinical challenge, we report a manganese-doped near-infrared quantum dot (QD) to intrinsically integrate the highly sensitive optical imaging with clinical compatible magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Taking the advantages of optical imaging powered by whole-brain clearing and cellular resolution three-dimensional (3D) panoptic imaging, in combination with the systematic in vitro cell studies on different types of cells involved in TBI, we disclosed the interpretable pathology reflected by TBI imaging through the highly sensitive fluorescence of magnetic QDs, i.e., after systemic administration, the nanoprobes were extravasated through the compromised blood-brain barrier and then selectively phagocytosed by activated microglia, which subsequently migrated into the regions rich in dead neurons and neuronal debris. This microglia-mediated tropism decodes the signal origin of MRI enhanced by the nanometer-sized contrast agent, thereby transforming the MRI from an anatomical tool into a pathological reporter. A biocompatible Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticle of similar size was also compared with the magnetic QD mentioned above for validating the translational merits of nanoparticles in MRI diagnosis of TBI.

title: Characterization of herpes B virus isolated from wild cynomolgus macaques and its pathogenic effects in captive hosts.
abstract: Despite the high seroprevalence of herpes B virus (BV) among wild macaques, it remains unclear why BV is rarely transmitted to humans who live alongside macaques in their natural habitats. We investigated disease progression, host immune responses, viral shedding, histopathology, and immunohistochemistry of tissues after BV injection in cynomolgus macaques. BV was isolated from a wild Thai cynomolgus macaque living in southern Thailand and intramuscularly injected into four captive macaques (two males and two females) housed at the Animal Biosafety Level 3 facility. Over 49 days, all macaques remained clinically healthy but showed enlarged lymph nodes. IgM was detected on 9 days post-infection (dpi) and peaked at 13 dpi, while IgG appeared on 11 dpi and peaked at 28 dpi. No viral DNA was detected in oral, urogenital, or rectal swabs throughout the 49 day study period. However, viral DNA was identified in the spleen, sublingual gland, and trigeminal ganglia. Histopathology revealed tissue damage in the spleen and trigeminal ganglion, with BV immunoreactivity in the spleen. Overall, BV injection induces localized lymphoid and immune responses without causing clinical symptoms or viral shedding in natural macaque hosts. This may help explain why natural macaque hosts remain healthy and why human BV infections associated with wild cynomolgus macaques have rarely been documented.IMPORTANCEHerpes B virus (BV) isolated from a wild cynomolgus macaque was inoculated into captive macaques in an experimental setting. BV infection triggers localized lymphoid and immune responses (IgM and IgG) without causing clinical symptoms or viral shedding. Viral DNA was detected in the spleen, sublingual gland, and trigeminal ganglia. These insights improve our understanding of how BV interacts with its natural macaque hosts and shed light on the rare transmission of BV from wild macaques to humans.

title: Predictors for Failure of Nonsurgical Treatment in Mild to Moderate Cubital Tunnel Syndrome.
abstract: Background: Activity modification to reduce mechanical stress on the ulnar nerve is an effective treatment for mild to moderate cubital tunnel syndrome (CuTS). However, some patients do not improve with nonsurgical management and ultimately require surgical intervention. This study aimed to identify predictors associated with nonsurgical treatment failure in CuTS. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed data from patients with CuTS classified as McGowan grades 1 and 2. Non-surgical management primarily consisted of activity modification, with adjunctive treatments including vitamin B12, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, pregabalin or mirogabalin and corticosteroid injections. Treatment failure was defined as the need for subsequent surgical intervention (transition-to-surgery group). The success group included 37 patients, and the transition-to-surgery group included 26 patients. Univariate and multivariate regression analyses were performed to evaluate predictors of nonsurgical treatment failure, including age, sex, body mass index, disease duration, comorbidities (diabetes mellitus, thyroid disease and radiographic cervical spondylosis) and concomitant elbow disorders (osteoarthritis, ganglion cysts and cubitus varus or valgus deformity). Elbow osteoarthritis was assessed radiographically using the Broberg and Morrey classification system. Results: Univariate analysis showed that corticosteroid injections, current smoking, radiographic cervical spondylosis and elbow osteoarthritis were more common in the transition-to-surgery group than in the success group. Multivariate analysis identified corticosteroid injections, radiographic cervical spondylosis and elbow osteoarthritis as independent predictors of nonsurgical treatment failure. Conclusions: Patients who received corticosteroid injections and those with radiographic cervical spondylosis or elbow osteoarthritis were more likely to experience nonsurgical treatment failure for mild to moderate CuTS and subsequently require surgical intervention. Early recognition of these risk factors may help clinicians identify patients who are less likely to respond to conservative management and consider earlier surgical treatment to prevent persistent symptoms and disease progression. Level of Evidence: Level IV (Therapeutic).

title: Low-Dose CT Lung-RADS 2022 for the Management of Screening- and Non-Screening-detected Lung Cancer Associated with Cystic Airspaces.
abstract: Background Lung cancer associated with cystic airspaces (CA) can be misinterpreted as a benign lesion, leading to missed or delayed diagnosis; however, the effect of the Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) 2022 criteria remains unverified. Purpose To retrospectively determine the frequency and outcomes of lung cancer associated with CA during screening and explore the potential effect of Lung-RADS 2022 on earlier diagnosis. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis included participants with lung cancers from three trials: the National Lung Screening Trial (2002-2007); Italian Lung Cancer Screening Trial, or ITALUNG (2004-2010); and German Lung Cancer Screening Intervention trial, or LUSI (2007-2016). Two radiologists jointly reviewed low-dose CT images to identify and morphologically characterize lung cancer associated with CA. Associations with histologic features, stage, and other variables were assessed. Lung cancer-specific survival was analyzed using Fine-Gray regression accounting for the competing risk of non-lung cancer death. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, stage, detection status, and trial. Lung-RADS 2022 criteria for atypical pulmonary cysts were applied. Results Seventy-three cancers associated with CA were identified in 1258 participants (median age, 64 years [IQR, 61-69 years]; 43 male), including 44 of 716 (6.1%) screening-detected and 29 of 542 (5.4%) non-screening-detected cancers. Multilocular morphologic type was associated with a more advanced stage than unilocular morphologic type (12 of 24 vs 15 of 49; P = .02). The 5-year lung cancer-specific survival was 51.4% (95% CI: 39.3, 62.3) for cancers associated with CA and 53.2% (95% CI: 50.1, 56.2) for 1054 participants with noncystic non-small cell lung cancer. No evidence of a difference in survival was observed (subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.15 [95% CI: 0.81, 1.63]; P = .44), and results remained consistent in multivariable models. Lung-RADS 2022 might have enabled earlier diagnosis in 55 of 73 cancers associated with CA (75%). Conclusion Lung cancer associated with CA accounted for 6.1% of screening-detected and 5.4% of non-screening-detected lung cancers. Outcomes were similar to those of noncystic non-small cell lung cancer, and Lung-RADS 2022 may facilitate earlier diagnosis. Clinical trial registration nos. NCT00047385, NCT02777996, and ISRCTN N30604390 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Byrne and Hammer in this issue.

title: Comparison of 7-T and 3-T MRI for the Detection of Multiple Sclerosis Lesions.
abstract: Background MRI is central to multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis. Although 7-T MRI improves lesion detection compared with 3-T MRI, systematic head-to-head comparisons across lesion locations and key imaging biomarkers, including the central vein sign (CVS) and paramagnetic rim lesions (PRLs), remain limited; consensus statements call for such studies to better define the clinical value of 7-T MRI. Purpose To systematically compare 7-T and 3-T MRI for detecting MS lesions across characteristic intracranial regions and key imaging biomarkers and to assess the incremental clinical value of 7-T MRI for lesion detection. Materials and Methods Patients with MS from the China National Registry of Neuro-Inflammatory Diseases were prospectively enrolled and underwent same-day 7-T and 3-T MRI examinations (March 2023 to June 2024). Images were anonymized and independently interpreted by two experienced raters in a blinded manner according to standard criteria. Lesion counts were compared with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test; inter- and intrarater reliability were assessed with the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Cohen κ, respectively. Results Among 30 participants (median age at MRI, 34.5 years [IQR, 30-48.3 years]; 27 female), 7-T MRI depicted more MS lesions overall than 3-T MRI (2268 vs 1779; relative increase, 27.5%; P < .001), with higher detection across cortical (+135.7%), juxtacortical (+26.1%), periventricular (+18.8%), and infratentorial (+33.5%) regions (all P < .001). Moreover, 7-T MRI visualized more CVS-positive lesions (1451 vs 592; +145.1%; P < .001) and more PRLs (634 vs 468; +35.5%; P < .001). The proportion of CVS-positive lesions was higher with 7-T MRI than with 3-T MRI (64.0% vs 33.3%, P < .001), whereas the proportions of PRLs were similar (28.0% vs 26.3%, P = .057). Interrater reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.99). Conclusion Compared with 3-T MRI, 7-T MRI improved MS lesion detection across characteristic intracranial regions and key imaging biomarkers, with a higher proportion of CVS-positive lesions but similar PRL proportions, supporting the clinical value of 7-T MRI. Clinical trial registration no. NCT05154370 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

title: Phase 2 Trial of 89 Zr-Deferoxamine-Daratumumab for CD38-targeted Immuno-PET/CT Detection of Multiple Myeloma.
abstract: Background Multiple myeloma (MM) imaging is currently suboptimal, which may limit patient care. Zirconium 89 ( 89 Zr) deferoxamine (DFO)-daratumumab is a novel CD38-targeted immuno-PET tracer. Purpose To compare 89 Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT against standard-of-care fluorine 18 ( 18 F) fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT for detection of MM. Materials and Methods Participants with MM were accrued to this prospective phase 2 trial between March 2022 and July 2025. Standard-of-care 18 F-FDG PET/CT and bone marrow biopsy were performed, along with research 89 Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT. If there were discrepant lesions between the two scans, image-guided biopsy was considered as the reference standard. The McNemar test was used to compare disease detection between the two imaging modalities. Results This study included 60 participants (median age, 63 years [IQR, 57-71 years]; 32 women). 89 Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT demonstrated at least one positive lesion in 43% (26 of 60; 95% CI: 31, 57) of participants, and 18 F-FDG PET/CT demonstrated at least one positive lesion in 47% (28 of 60; 95% CI: 33, 60) of participants. While there was no overall difference in disease detection between the two imaging modalities ( P = .81), MM was demonstrated only with 89 Zr-DFO-daratumumab PET/CT in 13% (eight of 60) of participants, with subsequent biopsy confirmation of active myeloma. Conclusion In participants with MM, CD38-targeted 89 Zr-DFO-daratumumab immuno-PET helped detect active myeloma in some participants with no signs of disease at 18 F-FDG PET/CT. Clinical trial registration no. NCT04814615 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Choyke in this issue.

title: Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Part-Solid Lung Adenocarcinomas with a Maximum Solid Portion Diameter of 30.0 mm.
abstract: Background The incidence of lymph node (LN) metastasis in patients with part-solid nodules (PSNs) is known to be low, which makes the intraoperative evaluation of LNs a controversial issue. Purpose To investigate the incidence of LN metastasis and explore clinical-radiologic predicting factors for LN metastasis in PSN lung adenocarcinomas with a solid portion diameter of 30.0 mm or less in a large surgical study sample. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included patients with part-solid lung adenocarcinomas with solid portion diameters of 30.0 mm or less on preoperative CT images from July 2023 to December 2024. For each PSN, overall tumor size, solid portion diameter, consolidation-to-tumor ratio (CTR), location, margin, shape, spiculation, lobulation, pleural retraction, bubble-like lucency, and air bronchogram were independently evaluated by two chest radiologists blinded to clinical information and pathology results. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Results This study included 1444 patients (median age, 59 years; IQR, 51-67 years; 931 women). The frequency of LN metastasis was 4.7% (68 of 1444 patients). None of the 115 patients with a CTR of 0.25 or less had LN metastasis (N1: 0 of 115; N2: 0 of 115). Rarely (0.2%, one of 552), LN metastasis was found in patients with a solid portion diameter of 6.0 mm or less. Solid portion diameter was the only independent predictor of LN metastasis (odds ratio, 1.25; 95% CI: 1.20, 1.31) in multivariable analysis and showed a superior diagnostic performance compared with CTR (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.86 [95% CI: 0.82, 0.90] vs 0.75 [95% CI: 0.68, 0.80]; P < .001), along with better calibration (Brier score, 0.039 vs 0.044) and greater net benefit. The clinical actionable cutoff for solid portion diameter was 7.3 mm (sensitivity, 95.6%; specificity, 49.6%). Conclusion Solid portion diameter had a superior diagnostic performance compared with CTR in predicting LN metastasis in patients with part-solid lung adenocarcinomas of solid portion diameter of 30.0 mm or less at CT. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

title: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors: Imaging Findings and a Multidisciplinary Approach to Treatment.
abstract: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) have evolved from historically misclassified smooth muscle tumors to a distinct disease entity, defined by gain-of-function mutations in KIT or PDGFRA proto-oncogenes. The advent of targeted therapy for this entity in the form of a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), imatinib mesylate, has transformed the treatment for GISTs, reducing recurrence and improving survival in patients with advanced disease. Radiologists play a critical role in initial lesion identification, surgical planning, and posttherapy surveillance, with cross-sectional imaging (CT and MRI) being vital in characterizing tumor features such as endophytic or exophytic nature, pseudocapsule, ulceration, necrosis, and changes in enhancement. Incorporating the Choi criteria into routine practice further refines response assessment, guiding adjustments in therapeutic strategy. A multidisciplinary approach is essential for optimal GIST management, requiring close collaboration between surgeons, oncologists, pathologists, and radiologists to establish a diagnosis, determine resectability, consider neoadjuvant or adjuvant TKIs, and monitor for disease recurrence (with imaging intervals tailored to risk classification). Future directions involve greater incorporation of molecular profiling to personalize treatments and the integration of newer-generation TKIs for imatinib-resistant cases, highlighting the continued importance of interdisciplinary coordination.

title: Primary Amenorrhea: Diagnostic Approach, Imaging Spectrum, and Common Pitfalls.
abstract: Primary amenorrhea is the absence of menarche in a 15-year-old adolescent girl who has developed secondary sex characteristics or a 13-year-old girl without development. Primary amenorrhea reflects disruption along the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian-uterine axis and may arise from a spectrum of anatomic, genetic, or functional abnormalities. Although primary amenorrhea is less common than secondary amenorrhea, recognition of the underlying level of dysfunction is essential for appropriate diagnosis and management as well as informed counseling regarding the patient's reproductive potential. A structured anatomic approach allows categorization of the causes into three levels based on the predominant site of dysfunction: level I, which involves the uterus and vaginal outflow tract; level II, which involves the ovaries and gonads; and level III, which involves the hypothalamus and pituitary gland. This classification system emphasizes a systematic and multidisciplinary approach to diagnosis and treatment, integrating clinical and biochemical testing and targeted imaging to localize the underlying dysfunction and guide treatment. Transabdominal US serves as the first-line imaging modality to help determine the presence and morphology of the pelvic organs. MRI provides detailed characterization of müllerian and urinary tract anomalies and allows evaluation of the hypothalamic-pituitary region when central causes are suspected.

title: Comprehensive Imaging Review of the Ureter.
abstract: The ureter is an important conduit between the kidney and the bladder and is frequently imaged to rule out cancer in the upper genitourinary tract. However, while malignancy can occur, a spectrum of other pathologic ureteral findings can exist, and these can be divided into congenital, intrinsic, and extrinsic abnormalities that range from postoperative and neoplastic conditions to inflammatory disease. This article provides a comprehensive overview of the ureter, including the ureteral anatomy, ureteral imaging strategies, and various ureteral conditions and their associated imaging features. It is important to identify congenital genitourinary variants, as these are frequently linked to further imaging recommendations, such as nuclear medicine renography and fluoroscopic voiding cystourethrography. Intrinsic abnormalities can be iatrogenic, infectious, inflammatory, or neoplastic. Intrinsic ureteral strictures are most commonly iatrogenic, usually resulting from prior surgery or radiation therapy. Ureteral infections include tuberculosis, schistosomiasis, and Escherichia coli infection, which have varying imaging manifestations. Inflammatory conditions include ureteritis cystica and pseudodiverticulosis. Ureteral masses are rarely benign and are most commonly urothelial carcinomas. Processes in the abdomen and pelvis, including mass effect from pregnancy, ureteral compression from advanced pelvic floor prolapse, and rarely, ureteral obstruction from vaginal devices, also can affect the ureter. The ureter can be injured during pelvic surgery or trauma. It also may be involved by deep pelvic endometriosis, mass effect from extrinsic lesions, or reactive change from inflammatory processes. Radiologists need to have a clear understanding of the patient's history and the range of possible ureteral conditions to establish the optimal differential diagnosis.

title: Imaging in Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma).
abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) or scleroderma is a multisystem autoimmune disorder characterized by a variable pattern of skin thickening and involvement of visceral organs. The pathophysiology is similar across all organs, which is chronic low-grade inflammation, with vasculopathy and eventual fibrosis. Diagnosis is primarily clinical, particularly in patients with established disease comprising characteristic skin and visceral manifestations, with a supportive role of laboratory and imaging findings. The presence of radiologic signs such as hidebound bowel or a combination of patulous lower esophageal sphincter, pulmonary fibrosis, skin thickening, and Raynaud phenomenon is relatively specific for SSc. Nevertheless, imaging in SSc is primarily used to determine the pattern, severity, and complications of visceral organ involvement, rather than for diagnosis of SSc. Radiologic evaluation in SSc employs a wide gamut of investigations, depending on the organ of interest. For example, US is used for the skin and superficial tissues; fluoroscopy, CT, or MR enterography for the gastrointestinal tract; endoanal US or MRI for the internal anal sphincter; high-resolution CT for the lungs; echocardiography and cardiac MRI for SSc-related pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and cardiac disease; and radiography, CT, or MRI for musculoskeletal involvement. Early diagnosis of treatable features, such as PAH and gastroesophageal reflux, can help reduce the morbidity and mortality associated with SSc. Imaging is additionally useful to prognosticate and monitor the disease. The authors focus on the multisystem, multimodality imaging manifestations of SSc with relevant differential diagnoses to bridge the gaps in knowledge about SSc. © RSNA, 2026.

title: 3D and 4D Hysterosalpingo-Contrast Sonography: Advanced Tubal Patency Assessment.
abstract: Female infertility affects approximately 15% of couples of reproductive age, with tubal disease responsible for up to one-third of cases. Therefore, accurate, minimally invasive evaluation of tubal patency is a cornerstone of fertility assessment. Among the available modalities, including hysterosalpingography (HSG), MR HSG, and laparoscopic chromopertubation, hysterosalpingo-contrast sonography (HyCoSy) has gained prominence as a valuable alternative to conventional methods due to its safety, accessibility, and diagnostic reliability. Recent advances in contrast-enhanced US involving the use of second-generation microbubble agents combined with three-dimensional (3D) and four-dimensional (4D) acquisition technologies have significantly improved the performance of HyCoSy. These developments enable real-time volumetric visualization of the uterine cavity and fallopian tubes, enhancing both anatomic delineation and functional assessment of tubal patency. In addition, combined 3D and 4D (3D-4D) HyCoSy enables complementary evaluation of uterine morphology, adnexal structures, and associated infertility-related disorders such as endometriosis and adhesions, facilitating a comprehensive "one-stop" reproductive imaging approach. This article is intended to serve as a practical guide to performing 3D-4D HyCoSy with microbubble contrast agents, including preparation, technical parameters, and findings interpretation. In addition, the authors compare HyCoSy with conventional techniques, review characteristic imaging patterns of tubal patency and occlusion, and discuss potential pitfalls and preventive strategies. As an advanced US technology combined with a dynamic functional perspective, 3D-4D HyCoSy represents a powerful, cost-effective, and patient-friendly tool for integrated fertility evaluation in modern radiology practices.

title: Imaging of Pediatric Pancreas Revisited: Spectrum of Diseases and Diagnostic Clues.
abstract: Pancreatic disease in pediatric patients includes a diverse range of congenital, inflammatory, traumatic, and neoplastic conditions. In this article, the authors provide a comprehensive overview of the imaging features of a broad range of pancreatic diseases in children, highlighting the roles of conventional and advanced imaging techniques while addressing pediatric-specific challenges. A structured review of pediatric pancreatic abnormalities, including the findings of US, CT, MRI with MR cholangiopancreatography, and nuclear medicine studies is presented. In addition, the benefits and limitations of these diagnostic imaging methods, as well as the necessity of a tailored, multimodality imaging paradigm for accurate diagnosis and management of pediatric pancreatic disease, are outlined. Emerging quantitative imaging methods have recently enabled objective evaluation of the pancreas at the cellular and molecular levels by means of assessment of the parenchymal volume, fat fraction, tissue stiffness, and microvascular architecture. In addition, radiomics and artificial intelligence models may enhance diagnostic accuracy by extracting large volumes of quantitative data from medical images to characterize tissue dimensions, morphology, and tissue heterogeneity. The authors provide a comprehensive review of the imaging findings of the most common neoplastic and non-neoplastic pediatric pancreatic diseases and their mimics. Finally, they outline the most common pediatric pancreatic surgical procedures, expected postoperative changes, and potential postsurgical complications to facilitate communication between the surgeon and the radiologist.

title: Role of MRI in Evaluating Lower Genitourinary Trauma: A Pictorial Review.
abstract: Diagnosis and management of lower genitourinary trauma presents substantial challenges to the complex anatomy and functional diversity of the affected organs. Imaging plays a critical role in accurately assessing the injury location and severity, guiding clinical decisions, and improving patient outcomes. US, CT, and conventional urethrography and cystography are commonly used for the initial assessment of patients with lower genitourinary trauma. MRI, with its superior soft-tissue contrast resolution and direct multiplanar imaging capability, is invaluable in selected cases of lower genitourinary trauma. MRI has a complementary role in diagnosis of acute penile fractures and testicular injuries when US findings are inconclusive, as MRI effectively delineates the tunica albuginea of the corpora of the penis as well as the testicles. Disruption of the tunica albuginea is an indication for immediate surgical repair. Traumatic urethral injuries can lead to strictures and disruptions, which often necessitate delayed reconstructive surgery. MRI has an adjunctive role in conventional urethrography and provides detailed anatomic information about the urethra and periurethral structures such as urethral stumps, urethral gap length, periurethral fibrosis, displacement of the prostate and rectum, fistulas, false channels, fractures and avulsions of the corporal bodies, and fluid collections such as hematoma, urinoma, and abscess. Bladder rupture with surrounding fluid collection can be identified at MRI, although confirmatory CT or conventional cystography may be necessary. Furthermore, MRI with and without intravenous contrast material is helpful for diagnosis of suspected partial segmental thrombosis of the corpus cavernosum. © The Author(s) 2026. title: 18 F-FET PET for Detection of Recurrent Disease in Gliomas: Tips and Tricks for Interpretation.
abstract: Gliomas are a heterogeneous group of primary brain tumors that are generally incurable. The current treatment paradigm for these tumors revolves around maximal safe resection and adjuvant chemoradiation; however, posttreatment changes can be difficult to distinguish from residual or recurrent disease. This makes it challenging to know whether treatments are working or the therapy should be escalated. Molecular imaging with amino acid PET has shown promise as a solution to this problem. The authors describe the interpretation considerations for the amino acid radiotracer fluorine 18-fluoroethyltyrosine (FET) in distinguishing posttreatment changes from recurrent glioma. The quantification of FET uptake on PET images and guidelines for interpretation are outlined.

title: Interpretable Artificial Intelligence for the Assessment of Mass Margin and Malignancy on Mammograms: A Reader Study.
abstract: Purpose To examine whether readers incorporate artificial intelligence explanations into their reasoning when assessing masses with mammography. Materials and Methods In an observer study, eight readers from April to August 2024 (four attending breast radiologists and four trainees) retrospectively interpreted 140 mammographic masses for malignancy. Readers were aided by a two-stage artificial intelligence system. The first stage classified mass margins, and the second estimated malignancy likelihood (0%-100%). Readers classified malignancy using two interfaces: a black-box interface providing only the malignancy score and an interpretable interface that also provided the margin assessment and a prototype-based explanation (based on a similar training mass). In both settings, malignancy scores were systematically underestimated. Regression analysis assessed reader-model agreement, and receiver operating characteristic curve analysis assessed diagnostic performance. Results Trainees agreed more often with interpretable margin categories (60.0% [337 of 560]) than black-box margin categories (43.9% [246 of 560]; Holm-Bonferroni adjusted P ( P holm ) < .001). When the model presented underestimated malignancy scores, trainees provided proportionally underestimated scores (β = 0.93; P holm < .001; 95% CI: 0.53, 1.33). Attending physicians also agreed more often with interpretable margin categories (interpretable, 55.0% [302 of 549]; black-box, 45.9% [257 of 560]; P holm < .001), but their malignancy scores were not associated with the model's bias (β = 2.00; P holm < .001; 95% CI: 1.40, 2.80). Malignancy performance showed no evidence of difference between interfaces for either trainees (black-box area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC], 0.75; 95% CI: 0.68, 0.82; interpretable AUC, 0.76; 95% CI: 0.72, 0.80; P holm = .64) or attending physicians (black-box AUC = 0.80; 95% CI: 0.75, 0.85; interpretable AUC = 0.77; 95% CI: 0.72, 0.83; P holm = .64). Conclusion Both trainees and attending physicians were influenced by the artificial intelligence model's mass margin assessment. However, only trainees were influenced by the black-box malignancy model's predictions. title: Management, Upgrade Rates, and Radiologic Surveillance of Screen-Detected High-Risk Breast Lesions.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the prevalence, upgrade rate, and radiologic surveillance management of high-risk lesions (HRLs) detected at screening mammography in a Dutch breast cancer screening population. Materials and Methods This retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained database included patients recalled from the Dutch breast cancer screening program between January 2009 and July 2019. Incidence rates, diagnostic work-up, radiologic surveillance, and upgrades to (pre)malignancy after surgical excision and during radiologic surveillance were evaluated. Results Among 17 809 recalled patients, 514 patients with a mean age of 58 years ± 8.1 (SD) were diagnosed with an HRL. The incidence rate of HRLs was 0.83 per 1000 screens and 2.89 per 100 recalls. The majority of HRLs consisted of papillary lesions (34.4% [177 of 514]) and atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) (31.1% [160 of 514]). Surgical excision was performed in 233 cases (45.3%), resulting in 58 HRLs (24.9%) being upgraded to (pre)malignancy. Invasive tumors were mainly found in papillary lesions with atypia and ADH. Of patients diagnosed with an HRL, 324 (63.0%) had an indication for radiologic surveillance. Of these, 257 (79.3%) underwent surveillance, with 109 (42.4%) completing the recommended 5-year surveillance trajectory. During surveillance, 26 patients (10.1%) developed a (pre)malignancy. Invasive tumors were more frequently identified among HRLs upgraded during surveillance than among HRLs upgraded after surgical excision (17 of 26 [65%] vs 16 of 58 [28%]; P = .001). HRLs upgraded to invasive cancer were more likely to be triple-negative compared with screen-detected cancers (9.1% [3 of 33] vs 6.6% [215 of 3277]; P < .001). Conclusion Overall, 16.3% (84 of 514) of screen-detected HRLs were associated with a diagnosis of (pre)malignancy after surgical excision or during radiologic surveillance. Completion of the recommended 5-year surveillance trajectory was achieved in fewer than half of patients undergoing surveillance. title: Comparison of Two Deep Learning Models and Their Combination for 1-year Lung Cancer Detection in Two Screening Cohorts.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the performance of Sybil, a Medical Open Network for Artificial Intelligence (MONAI)-based nodule model, and their combination for 1-year lung cancer detection in two screening cohorts: the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) and the Pamplona International Early Lung Cancer Action Program (P-IELCAP). Materials and Methods Baseline low-dose CT (LDCT) examinations from the NLST and the P-IELCAP were analyzed. A prespecified OR-stacked composite model combining Sybil, a MONAI-based nodule model, and a safety-net rule (MONAI-detected nodule > 6 mm with detection confidence > 0.95) was developed and evaluated for 1-year lung cancer detection. Model discrimination was assessed by using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and operating-point performance metrics were calculated. Results A total of 5110 baseline LDCT examinations were analyzed, including 2343 from NLST and 2767 from P-IELCAP, with 65 lung cancers diagnosed within 1 year. Mean age, mean pack-years, and percentage of female participants were 61.6 years ± 5.1 (SD), 57.3 pack-years ± 24.8, and 39.4% (923 of 2343), respectively, in NLST and 56.0 years ± 9.5, 34.4 pack-years ± 21.5, and 28.6% (791 of 2767), respectively, in P-IELCAP. Lung cancer incidence (per 1000 person-years) was higher in NLST than in P-IELCAP (17.7 vs 8.7; P = .006). Mean Sybil 1-year lung cancer probabilities (scaled by 1000 for presentation) were also higher in NLST than in P-IELCAP (16.4 vs 9.9; P < .01). Sybil achieved an AUC of 0.93 in both cohorts, whereas the MONAI-based model achieved AUCs of 0.90 in NLST and 0.79 in P-IELCAP. The composite model missed two of 65 1-year lung cancers while correctly classifying 2731 of 4965 (55.0%) noncancer examinations as negative, yielding a sensitivity of 63 of 65 (96.9%) and a positive predictive value of 63 of 2297 (2.7%). Conclusion For 1-year lung cancer detection with LDCT, the composite AI model achieved high sensitivity while maintaining acceptable specificity. Keywords: Applications-CT, Thorax, Pulmonary, Sybil, MONAI, NLST, P-IELCAP, Lung Cancer, Low Dose Computed Tomography Supplemental material is available for this article. © RSNA, 2026.

title: Spermidine improves fast-twitch muscle histopathology and specific-force, and select bone properties, in the mdx mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), an X-linked recessive disease, primarily affects skeletal and cardiac muscle, leading to progressive muscle wasting and weakness, but is also associated with compromised bone quality and microstructure. Human and mdx mouse studies show that DMD is associated with impaired muscle autophagy. The polyamine, spermidine, is known to stimulate autophagy, which some studies have linked to the upregulation of the microtubule-associated MAP1S protein. Spermidine has been shown to improve aspects of collagen VI deficiency-induced myopathy, in part, by reactivating autophagy. Thus, it was hypothesized that spermidine supplementation would improve the muscle pathology of DMD mdx mice, which would be associated with enhanced markers of autophagy and MAP1S. The impact of spermidine on bone quality or microstructure was also assessed using Synchrotron-generated x-ray imaging and 3-point bending. Three-week-old wild type (WT) and mdx mice were supplemented with 3 mM spermidine in drinking water for 13 weeks. Spermidine had no impact on mdx slow-twitch soleus muscle histopathology or contractile function, but improved mdx fast-twitch EDL muscle mass and specific tetanic force, which was associated with reduced centrally localized nuclei and tissue infiltrate. Surprisingly, despite a spermidine-induced increase in MAP1S protein, there was no change in markers of autophagy or autophagic flux. Finally, spermidine increased mdx femur trabecular tissue volumetric bone mineral density and bone volume fraction, with no impact on on bone mechanical properties. In summary, these preclinical data show that spermidine has therapeutic potential to improve muscle function in DMD and warrants further studies to investigate the underlying mechanism.

title: Presentation of Kaposi Sarcoma With Extensive Skin Lesions and Bone Involvement After Ten Years of Virally Suppressed HIV Infection and Restored CD4 Cell Counts.
abstract: Background Kaposi sarcoma (KS) is an HHV-8-associated angioproliferative tumor that can occur in persons living with HIV despite effective antiretroviral therapy. Although cutaneous KS after immune restoration has been described, extensive osseous involvement after prolonged viral suppression remains uncommon. Case presentation A 51-year-old man with HIV-1 infection and sustained viral suppression for more than 10 years presented with severe pain in the right foot, progressive swelling of the legs, and skin discoloration. Initial diagnostic considerations included gout, stasis dermatitis, and osteomyelitis. Persistent symptoms despite treatment prompted further investigation. MRI demonstrated multiple pathological bone lesions in both feet. Skin and bone biopsies subsequently confirmed HHV-8-positive KS involving the skin and bone. At diagnosis, the patient had a CD4 cell count of 750 cells/μL and a CD4/CD8 ratio of 1.42, with an undetectable HIV viral load. Treatment with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin resulted in a substantial clinical and metabolic response, but the patient experienced two subsequent recurrences. Symptomatic localized osseous progression of KS in the left foot was treated with radiotherapy, resulting in significant pain relief, while pegylated liposomal doxorubicin was continued with a favorable clinical and metabolic response. Conclusion This case highlights that extensive cutaneous and osseous KS can develop and recur despite prolonged viral suppression and restoration of conventional markers of immune function. KS should therefore remain in the differential diagnosis of unexplained cutaneous lesions, edema, and bone lesions in persons living with HIV, even when CD4 cell counts are preserved and HIV viral load remains undetectable. Long-term clinical surveillance and individualized multimodal treatment may be required.

title: Pancolitis due to Tuberculosis Masquerading as Inflammatory Bowel Disease in a 43-Year-Old Woman: Diagnostic Challenges in a Resource-Limited Setting-A Case Study and Literature Review From Ethiopia.
abstract: Background Gastrointestinal tuberculosis (GI TB) predominantly affects the ileocecal region, making primary colonic involvement exceptionally rare. In TB-endemic, resource-limited settings, differentiating colonic TB from inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-particularly Crohn's disease (CD)-presents a formidable diagnostic dilemma owing to overlapping clinical, radiological, and ileocolonoscopic features, often leading to diagnostic delays, misdiagnosis, and subsequent complications. Initial clinical presentation treatment and diagnostic re‐evaluation In May 2026, a 43-year-old Ethiopian woman presented to Jimma University Medical Center with a 10-month history of progressive colicky abdominal pain, chronic watery diarrhea, postprandial nonbilious vomiting, and significant weight loss. Prior empirical regimens of antihelminthic agents and broad-spectrum antibiotics administered at peripheral health facilities yielded no clinical improvement. Initial laboratory workup revealed microcytic hypochromic anemia (hemoglobin: 8.5 g/dL), a significantly elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) (92 mm/h), hypoalbuminemia (2.8 g/dL), and a normal carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) level (4 ng/mL). Ileocolonoscopy demonstrated superficial ulceration involving the ascending colon and hepatic flexure in a continuous form with numerous inflammatory polyps, and a small deep ulceration at the terminal ileum. Initial histopathology demonstrated chronic active inflammation without evidence of malignancy or granuloma formation. With a presumed diagnosis of CD, treatment was initiated with prednisolone and azathioprine, which might have contributed to the suspected deterioration of the clinical condition, warranting re-evaluation with contrast-enhanced CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis, which demonstrated diffuse, long-segment circumferential wall thickening involving the terminal ileum, the entire colon, and the rectum, alongside pericolic fat stranding, a mesenteric phlegmon, and multiple necrotic mesenteric lymph nodes, with the largest measuring 2 × 3 cm with peripheral rim enhancement. Fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) of the necrotic lymph nodes revealed epithelioid granulomas and characteristic caseous necrosis. With the above evidence, terminal ileitis and pancolitis due to TB were considered, immunosuppressive medications were discontinued, and standard antituberculosis therapy (2RHZE/4RH) was promptly initiated. The patient started to experience clinical improvement, achieving full resolution of her constitutional and abdominal symptoms and gaining weight at 1 month of follow-up. Conclusion Diagnosing GI TB-especially in atypical sites such as the colon-presents a critical challenge in resource-limited, TB-endemic settings, where differentiating it from IBDs, especially CD, is vital to prevent severe complications from inappropriate therapy. To avoid misdiagnosing GI TB as IBD (which risks disseminated infection from immunosuppression) or IBD as TB (which worsens bowel stricture, fistulae, and perforation), clinicians must perform mandatory pretreatment TB screening using radiologic, immunologic, molecular, and culture modalities before initiating immunosuppressive agents. Furthermore, diagnostic accuracy requires obtaining deep submucosal biopsies during ileocolonoscopy to detect characteristic granulomatous lesions if present. Finally, when an empirical anti-TB trial is necessary, it must be strictly time-limited and followed by objective re-evaluation at 8 weeks-including repeat endoscopy and biopsy-rather than relying solely on clinical symptomatic improvement.

title: Primary Pericardial Synovial Sarcoma Presenting as a Giant Intrapericardial Mass: A Case Report.
abstract: Primary pericardial synovial sarcoma is an extremely rare malignant tumor with nonspecific presentation and poor prognosis. We report the case of a 29-year-old woman whose pericardial mass was detected during a workplace health examination. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed a giant intrapericardial mass predominantly compressing the left atrium. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a heterogeneous intrapericardial mass extending from the left margin of the main pulmonary artery to the left atrioventricular groove, with partial invasion of the left atrial cavity. Ultrasound-guided biopsy showed a monophasic spindle-cell neoplasm. Immunohistochemistry showed focal weak positivity for pancytokeratin and epithelial membrane antigen, positivity for vimentin and D2-40, weak positivity for CD99, and a Ki-67 labeling index of approximately 15%. Fluorescence in situ hybridization using an SS18 break-apart probe demonstrated split red and green signals in tumor-cell nuclei, consistent with SS18 rearrangement. The patient declined surgical resection and adjuvant therapy and died 22 months after diagnosis. This case emphasizes that multimodality imaging is essential for defining tumor extent but cannot establish histological subtype. Integrated histology, immunohistochemistry, and SS18 fluorescence in situ hybridization are required for diagnostic confirmation.

title: Necrotic Immature Permanent Incisors: Apexification With Calcium Hydroxide and MTA Versus Pulp Revascularization: A Case Report With Long-Term Follow-Up.
abstract: Pulp necrosis in immature permanent teeth interrupts root development and prevents physiological apical closure, making endodontic management particularly challenging. Apexification with calcium hydroxide or mineral trioxide aggregate (MTA) has long been considered the standard treatment for these teeth by promoting the formation of an apical barrier and achieving periapical healing. However, neither approach allows continued root maturation, leaving thin dentinal walls that may compromise the long-term prognosis. Regenerative endodontic treatment, including pulp revascularization, has emerged as a biologically based alternative capable of promoting continued root development and reinforcing root structure. This report presents two clinical cases of necrotic immature permanent incisors managed at the Department of Pediatric Dentistry, CCTD Casablanca, Morocco, illustrating calcium hydroxide apexification, MTA apexification, and pulp revascularization. Both treatment approaches resulted in satisfactory clinical and radiographic healing. However, pulp revascularization demonstrated the additional benefit of continued root maturation, whereas apexification provided apical closure without further root development. These cases highlight the indications, advantages, limitations, and clinical outcomes of each therapeutic approach and support the current evidence favoring regenerative endodontic treatment whenever clinical conditions are suitable.

title: Conservative Management of a Cervical Horizontal Root Fracture in a Mature Permanent Incisor: A Case Report.
abstract: Cervical root fractures in permanent teeth are uncommon traumatic injuries that may present significant therapeutic challenges and are associated with a poor prognosis. This report describes the conservative management of a cervical horizontal root fracture in a permanent maxillary central incisor in a healthy 13-year-old girl who presented 48 hours after a sports-related trauma. Clinical examination revealed displacement and increased mobility of Tooth 21 and gingival bleeding. Periapical radiography showed a complete horizontal root fracture in the cervical third, at the level of the alveolar crest, with approximately 2 mm displacement between the fragments. The coronal fragment was repositioned and stabilized with a flexible splint fabricated from monofilament nylon fishing line and composite resin. A removable protective appliance was also provided during the initial 4 weeks to prevent premature contact and improve comfort. Considering the unfavorable prognostic factors, splinting was maintained for 7 months. At that time, localized gingival inflammation was observed around the splint, and the splint was removed. The gingival condition resolved within 1 week. Follow-up continued, and a mouthguard was subsequently provided for use during sports activities. At the 12-month follow-up, the tooth remained asymptomatic and functional, with maintained pulp sensibility and findings compatible with favorable healing. The natural tooth was preserved.
